method: two read-only auditors per article (facts; method and clarity), each finding checked by a skeptical second reader; refuted findings removed (42)

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:293 (change log, version 2): "...the clustered standard error of 4.41 pp in council_extended.json, t with 35 df as registered"
findings.problem: The change log says the t(35) reference used for the H4 CI and p is the registered one. The registered design specified Satterthwaite df, and moving to t(G−1) is listed in the design as a change made after estimation. This post-registration change is also missing from the article's own "What changed after registration" list.
findings.evidence: git show 3830f59:docs/research/prague-council-design.md line 159: "CR2 standard errors by sitting with Satterthwaite df". The current design's 'Changes after registration, 28 Sep 2026, after estimation' says: "H4 inference. CR2 uses a t(G − 1) reference instead of the Satterthwaite df, with G = 36 sittings." The #changes list (lines 230–235) does not mention it.
findings.fix: Change the log text to "t with 35 df (G − 1, changed from the registered Satterthwaite df after estimation)" and add a bullet to #changes: "28 September 2026, after estimation: H4 uses a t(G−1) reference instead of the registered Satterthwaite df; the wild cluster bootstrap agrees (p 0.536 vs 0.534)."
findings.note: Design §2 H4 (line 159) registers 'CR2 ... with Satterthwaite df'; 'Changes after registration' (line 328) records the switch to t(G−1). Change log line 293 says 't with 35 df as registered', and #changes (231–234) leaves the switch out.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:232: "three pieces were added after the results and are labelled as such in the text, namely the breakdown by which club says no, the one-dimensional scaling, and the comparison of lists in and out of government."
findings.problem: Only one of the three pieces was actually added after the results. The design registered the other two, outside the confirmatory family. The claim that the text labels them as post hoc is also untrue: no in-text sentence marks any of them that way.
findings.evidence: In the design, §2 H3 'Outside the family' lists "2PL IRT ideal points (one and two dimensions)", and RQ5 is headed "(exploratory, pre-registered)" with list yes shares by coalition status. Only "H3, exploratory. Added after the result: which clubs formed the 'not yes' side" is post hoc. The real post-registration deviation for the IRT is "One dimension only; two dimensions were not estimated", and it is not listed. Lines 164, 175 and 176 never say 'added after the results'.
findings.fix: Rewrite as: "28 September 2026, after estimation: the breakdown by which club says no was added after the results; the one-dimensional scaling and the comparison of lists in and out of government were registered as exploratory, but the two-dimensional scaling was not run." Also add "(added after the results)" next to fig. 5's first mention in the text.
findings.note: In the design, the IRT is listed 'Outside the family' under H3 (145–147), and RQ5 is headed 'exploratory, pre-registered' (164). Only the not-yes breakdown is marked 'Added after the result' (333). The article (164, 175, 176) never labels anything as added after the results; 176 says only 'reported as description'. The 'IRT one dimension only' deviation (337) is missing from #changes.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:102: "holds 2 468 votes over 42 sessions"
findings.problem: The design itself flags "42 sessions" as a miscount: it counts meeting dates, which split overnight sittings. The study's own units give 40 sittings (and 38 legal sessions), so 42 is inconsistent with the sitting count used for clustering elsewhere in the article.
findings.evidence: In design §0, Structure: "Sittings ... 41, 39, 43 and 40 per term. §0 of Part 1 said '42 sessions' for 2022–26: that count used meeting dates, which split overnight sittings." docs/research/prague-council-structure.json for 2022 gives sittings 40, legal_sessions 38. Only assets/zhmp/votes2022.json has "sessions": 42.
findings.fix: "holds 2 468 votes over 40 sittings (38 numbered sessions)", or "on 42 meeting days".
findings.note: votes2022.json 'sessions'=42 is datumjednani.nunique() in votes.py. The structure JSON gives 2022 as sittings 40 and legal_sessions 38. Design line 56 calls the 42 a count of meeting dates that splits overnight sittings.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:103: "For the current term they were checked against the clubs on the city's own list of councillors, and the only difference is Hana Kordová Marvanová"
findings.problem: The design records a second change in the current term that the article never mentions: Komrsková left the Pirates for "Jsme Team" in June 2026. The study keeps her in the Pirates as elected. That contradicts "the only difference" (the city list is cited as of September 2026). It also bears on the Pirates' club shares and on the robustness caveat at line 225.
findings.evidence: In design Appendix A, Club changes: "Komrsková left the Pirates for 'Jsme Team' in June 2026 (she stays in the club data as elected)." prague-council-sources.md, June 2026, cites prazsky.denik.cz. members2022.json has Komrsková Jana under Piráti for the full term. The article has no mention of Komrsková.
findings.fix: Add: "Jana Komrsková left the Pirates for Jsme Team in June 2026; she is kept in the Pirates' club, as elected, for the whole term." Then restate the comparison with the city's list accordingly.
findings.note: Design Appendix A and the sources note (line 29) both record Komrsková leaving the Pirates for Jsme Team in June 2026. members2022.json keeps her in Piráti, and the article never mentions her. I could not check whether the city's September 2026 list moved her club or only her party, so 'the only difference' can't be shown to be false.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:102: "...procedural votes, agenda changes and amendments, and in national parliaments those are the votes on which government and opposition fight most[8][9]"
findings.problem: The claim is attributed to sources that do not study national parliaments in general. Cox & McCubbins (2005) cover agenda control by the majority party in the US House. Carrubba et al. (2006) cover the selection bias of roll-call votes in the European Parliament. Neither establishes that, across national parliaments, procedural and amendment votes are where government and opposition fight most.
findings.evidence: Ref 8 is Setting the Agenda: Responsible Party Government in the US House of Representatives. Ref 9 is Carrubba et al., BJPS 36(4) 691–704, 'Off the record: unrecorded legislative votes, selection bias and roll-call vote analysis', on European Parliament roll calls. The design's §6 uses these sources more modestly: "That is where agenda control and opposition conflict are most visible".
findings.fix: "...and in the US House and the European Parliament, those unrecorded or procedural votes are where agenda control and conflict between majority and minority show most[8][9]."
findings.note: Ref 8 (Cox & McCubbins) is about the US House, and ref 9 (Carrubba et al. 2006) is about European Parliament roll calls; neither is a study of national parliaments in general. The design's §6 makes the narrower claim, with no 'national parliaments'.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:173 (fig. 5 caption) and 175: "Red: one or more clubs voted no as a whole"; "the coalition clubs almost never vote no ... ODS did so alone on 23 %"
findings.problem: The breakdown counts votes where a majority of a club's present members did not vote yes. That not-yes is mostly pressing nothing, not 'no'. The article itself says only 403 'against' entries were recorded this term and that non-yes is about 98 % nehlasoval. Calling these 'voted no' misdescribes the measure and contradicts the article's central distinction.
findings.evidence: council_extended.json H3_minority_clubs uses key 'clubs_not_yes'. The fig. 5 alt text says "had a majority not voting yes". votes2022.json how_clubs_say_no gives ANO Nehlasoval 0.981 and SPD 0.866.
findings.fix: Caption: "Red: one or more clubs had a majority not voting yes". Text: "the coalition clubs almost never withhold a yes as a club ... ODS alone withheld its yes on 23 %..."
findings.note: The fig. 5 caption at 173 defines the classes by 'a majority not voting yes' (JSON key clubs_not_yes), then says 'voted no as a whole'. Text 175 says 'vote no'. how_clubs_say_no gives ANO 98.1 % and SPD 86.6 % nehlasoval.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:200: "The lowest shares are on the budget (30 %) and on appointments (31 %)"
findings.problem: Organisational items have a lower share than appointments (30.57 vs 30.86), so the two lowest are budget and organisational, not budget and appointments.
findings.evidence: In assets/zhmp/council_extended.json H4.mean_nonsupport_by_category_pp: budget 29.99, organisational 30.57, appointments 30.86.
findings.fix: "The lowest shares are on the budget (30 %), organisational items and appointments (31 % each)".
findings.note: mean_nonsupport_by_category_pp: budget 29.99, organisational 30.57, appointments 30.86, so organisational is second lowest and is omitted.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:181: "three of the top five in SPD"
findings.problem: Fifth place is tied, so the count of SPD members in the top five depends on the tie-break. The data rank Urban (SPD) 27, Nerušil (SPD) 20, Čižinský (Praha sobě) 18 and Nekolný (ANO) 17. Rázga (ANO) and Seidl (SPD) then tie at 15, so the top five hold two or three SPD members.
findings.evidence: In assets/zhmp/members2022.json, 'against' counts: Urban 27, Nerušil 20, Čižinský 18, Nekolný 17, Rázga 15, Seidl 15.
findings.fix: "all three SPD councillors are among the six with the most votes against" or "two of the top four in SPD".
findings.note: members2022.json 'against' counts: Urban SPD 27, Nerušil SPD 20, Čižinský 18, Nekolný ANO 17, then Rázga ANO 15 and Seidl SPD 15. The top five holds two or three SPD members depending on the tie-break.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:110 and 149: "59 of them in 73 pairs of terms"; fig. 3 "21, 20 and 32 people"
findings.problem: The design's H1 eligibility, registered at 3830f59, says 74 transitions (22, 20, 32). The article and the results use 73 and 21 for 2010→2014, and the article never explains the drop of one.
findings.evidence: The design Appendix B H1 eligibility reads "74 consecutive-term transitions (22, 20, 32)". prague-council-structure.json h1_transitions gives 2010->2014: 22, including 'Novotný Petr', the 2010 column the crosswalk left unresolved. council_extended.json H1 gives transitions 73, by_pair 2010->2014 n 21.
findings.fix: Add a clause: "(73 of the 74 eligible pairs: one 2010 councillor, Petr Novotný, could not be matched to a list and is excluded)".
findings.note: Design line 313 gives 74 transitions (22, 20, 32). structure.json h1_pairs 2010->2014 has 22 names, including 'Novotný Petr', whom the code drops for a missing list (council_extended.py:133). JSON gives 73 and 21. The article never explains the drop.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:110 and 149: "average change in a councillor's log rate of voting against"; "0.49 times their own earlier rate"
findings.problem: The registered outcome is the change in logit((against+0.5)/(present+1)), so exp(mean D) is an odds ratio, not a ratio of rates or of log rates. At these tiny rates the difference is negligible, but the estimand is misnamed.
findings.evidence: Design §2 H1: "Δ_it = logit a_i,t+1 − logit a_it". council_extended.json gives mean_D −0.704 and ratio 0.495 = exp(−0.704).
findings.fix: "average change in the log odds of a councillor voting against" (line 110). You can keep "about 0.49 times their earlier rate" with a note that it is an odds ratio, close to a rate ratio at these low rates.
findings.note: Design §2 and council_extended.py:136/142 use the logit of (against+.5)/(present+1), so exp(mean_D) = 0.495 is an odds ratio. The article line 110 calls it a 'log rate'. The practical difference is negligible at these rates.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:207 (fig. 6 alt): "falling to under 10 % from late 2018, and near zero by 2026"
findings.problem: Several sittings after late 2018 are well above 10 %, so 'under 10 %' overstates the step.
findings.fix: "falling to mostly under 10 % from late 2018, with a few sittings up to about 30 %, and near zero by 2026".

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:200: "Opposition councillors present withheld a yes on 41 % of grant votes, 41 % of property votes and 37 % of land-use votes"
findings.problem: The quantity is the mean share of present opposition councillors who did not vote yes. It is not the share of votes on which the opposition withheld a yes, which the sentence implies.
findings.evidence: Design §2 H4 outcome: "The share of present opposition councillors ... who did not vote yes". council_extended.json mean_nonsupport_by_category_pp gives grants 41.1, property 41.45, planning 36.96.
findings.fix: "On average 41 % of the opposition councillors present withheld a yes on grant votes, 41 % on property votes and 37 % on land-use votes".
findings.note: In h4(), y is non.sum/pres.sum per vote, the share of present opposition councillors not voting yes, averaged over votes. The sentence at 200 reads as a share of votes.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:269–283 (references r2–r5, r8, r9, r13, r16)
findings.problem: The journal references carry no DOI, and most carry no page range, so they cannot be resolved directly. The Crossref metadata otherwise matches.
findings.fix: Append the pages and DOIs, e.g. r3 "98(2), 355–370. doi:10.1017/S0003055404001194", and likewise for r4, r5, r9 and r16.
findings.note: References 270–276 and 283 have no DOI, and only Holm (280) has a page range. No 'doi' string appears in the reference list apart from the Zenodo archive.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:164: "TOP 09 voted yes 91 % of the time while it led the city in 2011–14"
findings.problem: From November 2011 to May 2013 TOP 09 was the junior partner in a coalition under an ODS mayor (Svoboda). It led the city only from June 2013 (Hudeček).
findings.evidence: Design Appendix A: 24 Nov 2011 – 23 May 2013 ODS + TOP 09, mayor Svoboda; 20 Jun 2013 to end of term TOP 09 minority council, mayor Hudeček. RQ5 TOP 09 coalition yes shares are 0.911 and 0.913.
findings.fix: "TOP 09 voted yes 91 % of the time while it governed in 2011–14".
findings.note: The RQ5 TOP 09 coalition yes share of 0.911 is for 24 Nov 2011 – 23 May 2013. Appendix A has ODS + TOP 09 under mayor Svoboda (ODS) in that period, with TOP 09 leading only from 20 Jun 2013.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:181 "The three lowest attendance records ... account for most of the dips in its quarterly agreement with SPOLU, when its members were absent and did not vote against." (also :133)
findings.problem: The attribution of Praha sobě's agreement dips to absences contradicts the measure. A club's side is computed only among its members who are present, so absent members cannot move it. No code computes the share of the dips that these three councillors account for. The quarterly chart has also been cut, so readers cannot see the 'dips'.
findings.evidence: tools/zhmp/votes.py:99-106 positions(): share = yes / present members (absent excluded), pos = share > 0.5. agreement_with_spolu_by_quarter (votes.py:148) is the only quarterly computation, and nothing in tools/zhmp or tools/charts decomposes it by councillor. Changelog line 293 confirms the quarterly chart (former fig. 2) was cut.
findings.fix: Delete the attribution, or compute it (agreement by quarter with and without the three members) and report the numbers. If kept, say the dips come from present members pressing nothing (line 133), not from absence: 'In those quarters a third of the club's present members pressed nothing, which put the club's side at not-yes; absences do not enter the club's side.'
findings.note: votes.py positions() computes the club side as yes/present members, so absences cannot move it. No code splits the quarterly agreement by councillor. Line 181 attributes the dips to absences, which conflicts with line 133 (present members pressed nothing).

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:149-154 (H1 section) and :241 "not a steady halving in each term"
findings.problem: The registered secondary outcome for H1, explicit non-support, was computed but not reported. The design lists it under 'Reported with it'. Its pattern runs against the article's framing: a clear fall in every transition, not one concentrated in 2010–14. Leaving out a registered outcome whose result differs from the headline is selective reporting, and it is not disclosed in 'What changed after registration'.
findings.evidence: docs/research/prague-council-design.md:101-104 ('explicit non-support as a secondary outcome'). council_extended.json H1_explicit_nonsupport: ratio 0.345, p 1e-05; by transition 0.274 (CI −1.73 to −0.86 logit), 0.287 (−1.70 to −0.80), 0.483 (−1.01 to −0.44), all excluding zero.
findings.fix: Report it beside H1, e.g. 'On the registered secondary outcome, the share of a councillor's present non-yes votes recorded as against or abstain, the same people fell in every transition (×0.27, ×0.29, ×0.48); this mostly reflects the post-2018 fall in abstaining.' Or list its omission as a deviation.
findings.note: Design line 104 lists 'explicit non-support as a secondary outcome' as reported with H1. H1_explicit_nonsupport exists in the JSON (0.274, 0.287, 0.483; pooled 0.345). The article never mentions it, and #changes does not list it.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:210 "This analysis was registered as description, so no test is claimed for it." and "steps down further than that trend alone would produce"
findings.problem: The H2 model specified in the design was estimated, including its bootstrap p-values, but the article reports neither the estimate nor the design's decision label. It asserts the result in words only ('steps down further than that trend alone would produce'). Several registered H2 outputs were never run, and neither the article nor the design lists them as not run: the sup-F and Elliott–Müller break sets, the check of within-term breaks against 15 Oct 2020, and the §5.2 robustness checks (6 h and 20 h sitting gaps, flagged rows, votes after midnight, COVID sittings).
findings.evidence: council_extended.json H2: all_members gamma −0.332, p 0.0001; continuing_members gamma −0.283, p 0.0002 (n = 20); official_totals gamma −0.101, p 0.0004. council_extended.py main() has no sup-F or break-date code. The robustness.not_run list omits these items. Design :116-121 and §5.2.
findings.fix: State the estimate: 'The registered jump model puts the step at −33 points of the abstain share (−28 among the 20 continuing councillors), against separate within-term trends.' Then add the unrun sup-F, break-date and §5.2 checks to 'What changed after registration'.
findings.note: The JSON holds H2 gamma −0.332 (p 0.0001), −0.283 among continuing members and −0.101 on official totals. The article gives none of these numbers or the decision label. council_extended.py has no sup-F, Elliott–Müller, break-date or §5.2 code, and neither robustness.not_run nor the design's not-run list names them.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:232 "three pieces were added after the results and are labelled as such in the text, namely the breakdown by which club says no, the one-dimensional scaling, and the comparison of lists in and out of government"
findings.problem: The deviations list is wrong in both directions. (1) The one-dimensional IRT and the list comparison by coalition status (RQ5) were pre-registered, as 'outside the family' and as 'exploratory, pre-registered'; they were not added after the results. (2) The real deviations are not listed: the two-dimensional IRT and APRE were not estimated, RQ5 was registered 'with intervals' and with the against rate and a comparison to lists that never switch, none of which is reported, and the H4 degrees of freedom were changed from Satterthwaite to t(G−1). That last change is disclosed in the design file only. (3) Neither section 'labels as such in the text' the fig. 4 and fig. 5 analyses as post-registration.
findings.evidence: Design :145-150 (2PL IRT one and two dimensions, APRE), :164-168 (RQ5 with intervals), :328-337 (H4 t(G−1); 'IRT. One dimension only'). Article :158-176 contains no 'added after the results' wording.
findings.fix: Rewrite the bullet: 'Added after the results: which clubs formed the not-yes side (fig. 5). Pre-registered but changed: the IRT was run in one dimension only, without APRE; the list comparison (fig. 4) is reported without the registered intervals and against-rate measure; H4 uses t with 35 df instead of Satterthwaite (the wild bootstrap agrees, p 0.536).' Label fig. 5 in its section as post-registration.
findings.note: Same as [1]: the IRT and RQ5 were registered. The deviations missing from #changes are 2-D IRT/APRE not run (337), RQ5 without intervals or comparison lists (168), and H4 df (328). The fig. 4 and fig. 5 text has no post-hoc label.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:234 "not run: a conditional logit and bounds ..., alternative contested-vote cut-offs (H3), and an audit against complete session records"
findings.problem: Many registered robustness analyses were neither run nor disclosed. For H3: lrgen and galtan as alternative axes for 2018–22, excluding the 2026 rows with missing seats, and nehlasoval coded as missing. For H4: each category's keywords dropped in turn, a Firth logit, the 2018–22 replication, the same model for coalition councillors, and the difference-in-differences. For H4 the council-only stratum versus councillor- and committee-proposed items is also not reported.
findings.evidence: Design §5 items 2-4 and :162-163. council_extended.py implements none of them, and its robustness.not_run list does not include them.
findings.fix: Extend the not-run bullet to list each of these, or run them.
findings.note: Design §5.3–5.4 and line 162 register checks that are not in council_extended.py and not in not_run, and that the article does not list. Missing: lrgen/galtan alternatives, excluding the 2026 rows, keyword drop-one, Firth, 2018–22 replication, the coalition-councillor model, the DiD, and the councillor/committee stratum. (Nehlasoval-as-missing does appear in the design's not-run list but not in the article's line 234.)

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:119 "not supported · left–right cut fits better"; :170; :176 "The main line in the assembly therefore runs between government and opposition"
findings.problem: The results table says the left–right cut 'fits better'. Yet the text itself explains (:175) that the left–right rule picks the best of all cuts on every vote while the coalition rule is fixed, so the comparison favours left–right by construction. The section then draws the opposite substantive conclusion ('therefore runs between government and opposition') from the descriptive one-dimensional scaling, an analysis outside the family, stated as a firm finding. The registered test and the descriptive conclusion contradict each other, and neither the table nor the tl;dr flags this.
findings.evidence: council_extended.py:280-282 (rule a: min over 2 directions; rule b: min over every cut and both directions, including trivial ones). H3 p = 1.0 in both periods. IRT club means are description only (design :145).
findings.fix: Table cell: 'not supported; the test lets the left–right rule choose its cut on each vote, which favours it'. At :176 write 'The descriptive scaling suggests the main line runs between government and opposition', and note that this is not a test.
findings.note: Narrowly confirmed. Line 175 already discloses the asymmetry (code 280–282: rule b takes the min over all cuts, including trivial ones). Line 176 still draws a firm conclusion ('therefore runs between government and opposition') from descriptive IRT, and the table and tl;dr carry no flag.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:69-78 details.tldr
findings.problem: The short version leaves out the single supported result (×0.49 within the same councillors, p < 0.001, 59 people) and what it rests on (adjustment for coalition status, 55–67 % of roll calls). It does not say what would overturn it, for example that the effect disappears among status-stable councillors and depends on one transition. The first bullet ('The fall in votes against comes mostly from the first change of term') does not say whether it means the assembly-wide fall or the within-councillor estimate. The most useful practical sentence, that the record now tells a reader less about who opposed what than in 2010, is buried at :144.
findings.evidence: tldr bullets :72-76 contain no number. Shift-share and H1 are both 'mostly first transition', but for different reasons (council_extended.json shift_share vs H1.by_pair).
findings.fix: Lead with: 'The same councillors voted against about half as often in each new term (×0.49, 59 people), but almost all of that is 2010–14 and depends on adjusting for moves between coalition and opposition; among those who never switched it is ×0.86, not significant. Disagreement is now recorded mostly as pressing nothing, so the record says less about who opposed what. The files hold 55–67 % of roll calls.'
findings.note: tl;dr bullets 72–76 contain no numbers and do not state the ×0.49 result. 'The fall in votes against comes mostly from the first change' doesn't say whether it means the aggregate fall or the within-person fall. Note that the 'depends on adjustment' part of the suggested fix is overstated (see [15]).

findings.problem: Several technical terms appear without explanation at first use. 'family-wise error rate' and 'Holm's procedure' (:108). 'estimand', 'log rate' and 'sign-flip test' (:110; sign-flip again at :149). 'pp' and 'one-sided p' (:120). 'classification errors' (:119). 'contested votes' (first used :169, defined only in the fig. 5 caption, :173). 'bootstrap by sitting' (:170). 'one-dimensional scaling', with scores such as +0.96 or −1.10 given without stating the scale (standardised, mean 0, SD 1, sign fixed by the mayor) (:176). 'standard errors clustered by sitting' and 'κ' (:200). The sign-flip test and the scaling scores are central and have no example or gloss.
findings.evidence: Read of the article text: none of these terms is glossed before or at first use.
findings.fix: Add short glosses, e.g. ':110 sign-flip test — how often a result this negative appears if each person's change is randomly given the opposite sign'; ':176 scores are standardised (mean 0, SD 1) positions, positive on the mayor's side'; define 'contested' (at least 2.5 % of present members on the losing side) in the text at :169.
findings.note: 'Contested' is first used at 169 and defined only in the fig. 5 caption (173). The sign-flip test, Holm, FWER, 'pp' and the IRT score scale are used without a gloss (108, 110, 120, 176).

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:149 "It uses only votes against, because they need a button press, so no change in how the system records a member who presses nothing can move them."
findings.problem: This overstates how robust the measure is. The rate is against / present, and 'present' includes nehlasoval. A change in whether a logged-in member who is out of the room is recorded as nehlasoval or chyběl changes the denominator and therefore the rate.
findings.evidence: council_extended.py:136 ra = (against + .5) / (present + 1); council.PRESENT includes 'Nehlasoval' (votes.py and design :180).
findings.fix: '... so such a change cannot move the count of votes against, though it can move the number present that the rate is divided by.'
findings.note: council.PRESENT includes 'Nehlasoval', and the H1 rate divides by present+1. A recording change between nehlasoval and chyběl therefore moves the denominator. Line 149 says no such change 'can move them'.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:110 "the average change in a councillor's log rate of voting against"; :149 "0.49 times their own earlier rate"
findings.problem: The code works on the logit of a smoothed rate, (against + 0.5) / (present + 1), not on the log rate, so exp(mean) is an odds ratio of smoothed rates and averages are weighted equally per person. At rates near 1 % the difference is small, but the description is not what the code does.
findings.evidence: council_extended.py:108-109, :136, :142, :150, :159; design :93-94 (logit).
findings.fix: 'the average change in the log-odds of a councillor's (smoothed) rate of voting against, each person weighted equally'.
findings.note: Duplicate of [9]. Code lines 136, 142 and 150 use the logit of the smoothed rate and an equal-weight person mean.

findings.location: texts/prague-council.html:154 "among the 26 people whose coalition status never changed" and :222
findings.problem: The code defines a 'stayer' as a change of less than 0.5 in the share of seated votes spent in opposition, not as a status that never changed, so partial switchers are included.
findings.evidence: council_extended.py:143 "stayer": abs(y.opp_share - x.opp_share) < 0.5.
findings.fix: 'whose share of the term spent in opposition changed by less than half' or recode the stayers as exactly unchanged.
findings.note: council_extended.py:143 has stayer = abs(Δopp_share) < 0.5, which includes partial switchers. The article (154, 222, 225) says 'never changed / did not change'.

findings.location: texts/prague-rings.html:159 "The design-stage power check had predicted this, since with 282 clusters the standard error was bound to be larger than the margin."
findings.problem: The reason given for the inconclusive H2 does not match the estimates. The SE actually used, 0.137, is well below the ±0.25 margin. The design-stage figure of 0.31 was a pessimistic precinct-SD projection, and the realised SE did not exceed the margin. The test is inconclusive because the point estimate (−0.17) sits close to −0.25 and the 90 % CI reaches −0.40, not because the SE exceeded the margin.
findings.evidence: assets/praha/rings_extended.json H2: se_used 0.1372, margin 0.25, ci90_used [-0.3975, 0.0539]; docs/research/prague-rings-power.json h2.se_log2_metro_pp 0.311 (design-stage projection); prague-rings-design.md:305 'SE ... about 0.31 pp per doubling, above the ±0.25 margin'.
findings.fix: "The design-stage power check had expected this test to have almost no power. The realised standard error (0.14) is smaller than projected, but with a point estimate of −0.17 the 90 % interval still reaches −0.40, past the margin."
findings.note: rings_extended.json H2 se_used 0.1372 < margin 0.25. The 0.31 in design l.305 is the pessimistic projection. The article's l.159 'SE was bound to be larger than the margin' does not hold for the realised SE. Inconclusive because estimate −0.17 and CI90 reaches −0.3975.

findings.location: texts/prague-rings.html:131 (H1b′ row: "not supported · θ = 0.42, p = 0.91") and :148 "For SPOLU the pattern is the same and weaker, with 42 % explained and neither direction significant."

It also pre-committed that an 'indeterminate' H1b would be reported as 'underpowered'. SPOLU's outcome is 'indeterminate', yet the article never uses either the registered outcome label or 'underpowered'. It reports only 'not supported'.
findings.evidence: rings_extended.json H1_SPOLU.outcome_unadjusted = "indeterminate", wild p greater 0.0881 / less 0.912; prague-rings-design.md:58-61 (three outcomes) and :303-304 'As pre-committed, an "indeterminate" H1b is reported as underpowered, never as "place"'.
findings.fix: Change the H1b′ result cell to "not supported (indeterminate: underpowered, as pre-committed)" and the text to "...with 42 % explained and neither direction significant, which the design pre-committed to report as underpowered."
findings.note: H1_SPOLU.outcome_unadjusted = 'indeterminate'. Design l.304: 'an indeterminate H1b is reported as underpowered'. The article shows only 'not supported' (l.131) and 'neither direction significant' (l.148), never the registered label or 'underpowered'.

findings.location: texts/prague-rings.html:159 "The design-stage power check had predicted this, since with 282 clusters the standard error was bound to be larger than the margin... with 282 clusters a negligible metro effect cannot be told from a small one." (also l.205 "underpowered from the start")
findings.problem: The text gives the wrong reason for H2 being inconclusive. The standard error the test actually used is 0.137 pp, about half the ±0.25 margin, not larger than it. The test fails because the point estimate (−0.17) lies close to −0.25, not because 282 clusters make equivalence impossible. The design-stage figure of about 0.31 came from a pessimistic precinct-residual assumption that the realised data did not bear out.
findings.evidence: assets/praha/rings_extended.json H2: se_used 0.1372 (largest of hc1 0.1372, cr2 0.1421, conley 0.1306, wild 0.1329), estimate −0.1718, ci90_used [−0.3975, 0.0539], p_tost 0.2843. Design doc §5a: "SE of the metro coefficient at the cluster level is about 0.31". With SE 0.137, an estimate near 0 would have passed TOST (the 90% CI would be ±0.23).
findings.fix: Replace with: "The design-stage check, using a pessimistic residual variance, expected a standard error of about 0.31, above the margin. The realised one is 0.14, so the test could have passed. It does not, because the estimate itself, −0.17, lies close to the −0.25 margin: the data lean towards a small negative association (ANO slightly stronger near stations) rather than towards none." Drop "cannot be told from a small one" as a property of the sample size.
findings.note: Duplicate of [0]: realised SE 0.137 (max of hc1/cr2/conley/wild is cr2 0.142, but se_used is 0.1372). TOST would pass for an estimate near 0 (CI ±0.23). l.159 attributes the failure to the cluster count and SE > margin, which the realised SE does not support. l.205 'underpowered from the start' is correct as a description of the design stage.

findings.location: texts/prague-rings.html:148 "Of the gradient, 57 % survives, and the test in the other direction, whether more than half is left, rejects at p = 0.03."; table l.130 "not supported"
findings.problem: The design registered three outcomes for H1b: "composition", "place beyond composition" and "indeterminate". The code's registered outcome for ANO is "place beyond composition", but the article never names it. It reports only "not supported", plus the reverse-direction p-value with no label, and the summary (l.216) reframes the remainder as "cannot be credited to the estates as places". This is a registered label left unreported, and the change does not appear in "What changed after registration". The p = 0.03 also rests on the wild bootstrap alone: HC1 and Conley give 0.061 and 0.063, which the text does not say.
findings.evidence: rings_extended.json H1_ANO.outcome_unadjusted = "place beyond composition"; delta.p.wild.greater 0.0281, cr2 0.0386, hc1 0.0608, conley_1.5km 0.0626. tools/praha/rings_extended.py:267-268 computes the label. Design §2 H1b lists the three declared outcomes. Design §7 says a "place" result is to be read as an upper bound on the place effect.
findings.fix: Add to l.148 and to the results table: "Under the registered decision rule this is the outcome 'place beyond composition' (θ significantly below one half and the remaining gradient above zero). The reverse test gives p = 0.03 with the bootstrap and 0.04 with CR2, but 0.06 with conventional and spatial errors. Since unmeasured income, tenure and length of residence could carry the remainder, 'place' here means only 'not explained by education and citizenship'." If the label is deliberately not used, record that under "What changed after registration".
findings.note: H1_ANO.outcome_unadjusted = 'place beyond composition' (design l.60 rule). The article gives the reverse p = 0.03 but never the registered label. p.greater: wild 0.0281, cr2 0.0386, hc1 0.0608, conley_1.5km 0.0626, so 'rejects at p = 0.03' rests on wild/CR2 only.

findings.location: texts/prague-rings.html:68-74 details.tldr, bullet "Education and citizenship explain part of ANO's estate gradient; with age added, about half."
findings.problem: The short version gives no numbers and does not say what the result rests on: 282 one-kilometre census clusters, 56 districts as the effective sample, aggregate rather than individual data. It also does not say what would overturn the result. Its composition bullet leads with the age-added figure (52 %), which the design calls descriptive and possibly over-controlling, instead of the registered result: 43 %, not supported, with more than half the gradient significantly remaining. The one result that passes Holm (steepening, +0.26) is given no number and is not marked as the only confirmed one.
findings.evidence: Design §1: "The primary composition block is education + citizenship. Age is added in a second step and reported descriptively." rings_extended.json holm: only H3 rejects. The tldr ul at l.69-75 contains no figures, sample size or falsifier.
findings.fix: Rewrite, e.g.: "ANO takes 26 % where most flats are panel, 16 % where few are. Census education and citizenship account for 43 % of that gap: less than the registered half, and the rest remains significant (adding age, which may over-control, gives 52 %). The one test that passes after correction: the gap grew from 0.55 to 0.80 pp per 10 pp of panel flats between 2017 and 2025, in older precincts. All of this rests on 1 km census squares and 56 districts; finer census data showing a much larger composition share would overturn the 43 %. The metro and turnout tests are inconclusive."
findings.note: The tldr (l.69-74) contains no numbers. The composition bullet gives 'part' for the registered block and highlights the age-added 'about half', which the design treats as descriptive. It does not mark H3 as the only Holm-passing result.

findings.location: texts/prague-rings.html:149 "The direction is not guaranteed here, because ... the allocation error is correlated with the housing measure itself; 43 % is therefore likely understated, not a proven lower bound." (repeated in summary l.216 "likely understated")
findings.problem: Non sequitur. The sentence gives the reason the attenuation-bias direction cannot be assumed, then concludes "therefore likely understated". No analysis in the article or the code establishes the direction, so the summary claims more than the analysis supports.
findings.evidence: Design §7 assumed classical measurement error ("a 'composition' result is conservative"). The article itself withdrew that (change log l.210, l.269). No simulation or check of the allocation-error direction appears in tools/praha/rings_extended.py or rings_robust.py. The only related evidence is the single-precinct robustness (θ 30 %), which concerns resolution, not allocation error.
findings.fix: Either cite the evidence for "likely" (for example: "at coarser resolution θ falls, from 43 % in clusters to 30 % in single precincts, which suggests finer composition would raise it") or write "43 % may be understated or overstated: coarse census squares would normally understate it, but because census counts were spread by flats, the error is tied to the housing measure and its direction is unknown". Change l.216 accordingly.
findings.note: l.149 argues the direction is not guaranteed, then concludes 'therefore likely understated'. Nothing in the article or the change log (l.210) gives evidence for the direction, so the 'therefore' does not follow. Repeated at l.216.

findings.location: texts/prague-rings.html:59, 62, 63 (hero) and l.95 "how much of the estates' gradient is left"
findings.problem: The central term "estate gradient" is used in the subtitle, two hero stats and the introduction before it is defined. Its unit (pp of party vote per 10 pp more flats in panel buildings, holding distance from the centre, the metro and family houses equal) first appears implicitly at l.112 and in the hero only as "pp per 10 pp". The hero stats also use "registered block" (l.62) and "administrative count" (l.61) without explanation. "Registered block" is explained only at l.143, and "administrative count" is never explained.
findings.evidence: grep: "estate gradient" first at l.59/62; the definition-like sentence "Every ten percentage points of panel flats go with 0.9 pp more for ANO" is at l.112. "administrative count" appears only at l.61.
findings.fix: At first use (l.59 or in the hero) add: "the estate gradient: how many points ANO gains for every 10 percentage points more flats in panel buildings, other measures held equal". Replace "registered block" in the hero with "education and citizenship (registered)". Drop "administrative count" or say what it means ("cadastre count of flats").
findings.note: grep: 'estate gradient' appears in the meta, l.62 and l.63 before any definition. 'Administrative count' occurs only at l.61 and is never explained. 'Registered block' in the hero is unexplained.

findings.location: texts/prague-rings.html:120 "wild cluster bootstrap by city district", "small-sample-corrected", "spatial standard errors", "Holm's procedure"; l.132 "equivalence (TOST)"; l.135 and l.174 "elasticity"; l.169 "family-wise threshold"; l.191-194 "fractional logit", "spatial error model", "Moran's I", "Hausman test"; l.138 "θ" used in table rows l.130-131 before the note defines it
findings.problem: Technical terms are used without a plain-language gloss at first use. For a general reader, "TOST" and "elasticity" are the ones that matter, because they carry the H2 and H4b results.
findings.evidence: None of these terms has an explanatory clause at the cited lines. θ is defined only in the note below the table (l.138), after it appears in the rows.
findings.fix: Add short glosses: "wild cluster bootstrap (resampling whole districts, so that neighbouring precincts are not treated as independent)"; "equivalence test (TOST: both ends of the interval must lie inside ±0.25)"; "elasticity (the % rise in envelopes for a 1 % rise in the register)"; "Holm's procedure, which tightens the threshold for each of the six tests". Move the θ definition above the table.
findings.note: θ is used in table rows l.130-131 and defined only in the note at l.138. TOST, elasticity, Holm and wild cluster bootstrap carry no plain-language gloss at first use. Clarity, low.

findings.location: texts/prague-rings.html:119 "Everything that changed afterwards is listed below." / l.202-210 "What changed after registration"; l.164 and l.174
findings.problem: The deviation list and the results leave out several registered or registered-adjacent items. (1) The design's own change log records CR2 with a t(G−1) reference instead of Satterthwaite df; the article does not. (2) Design §3 says H4a and H4b are "reported with" the flagged precincts; the article does not report them, and with flagged precincts included H4b gives elasticity 0.74, p = 0.013. (3) Design §4 asks for matched and unmatched precincts to be compared by distance and 2025 vote, and for the 57-district comparison; only the panel share is reported. (4) H3 applies the 2025 housing stock to the 2017 vote, which the text describes only as "holds housing fixed".
findings.evidence: docs/research/prague-rings-design.md "2026-09-28, estimation": "CR2 ... with a t(G − 1) reference instead of the Satterthwaite df". rings_extended.json H4_with_flagged.h4b: estimate 0.7428, p.wild.less 0.0133. H3_sensitivity.matched_vs_not includes log2_centre and ano_2025_share (18.2 vs 20.5 %), which are unreported. tools/praha/rings_extended.py:318-345: h3() uses s.panel_flats (current stock) for both years.
findings.fix: Add the CR2 reference change to the deviation list. Add one sentence to the turnout section: "With the flagged precincts kept, as registered for reporting, the elasticity is 0.74 (p = 0.01), equally uninterpretable for the same reason." Extend l.164 with distance and ANO 2025 share for matched and unmatched precincts. State that the 2017 and 2021 models use today's housing stock.
findings.note: The design change log (l.319) records CR2 with a t(G−1) reference; the article's deviation list (l.202-210) omits it. Design l.147 says H4 is 'reported with' the flagged precincts; H4_with_flagged exists in the JSON but is absent from the article. matched_vs_not has log2_centre and ano_2025_share (18.2 vs 20.5), unreported. The 2025 housing stock is applied to 2017 (h3 uses panel_flats); the article says only 'holds housing fixed'.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:69 "the design could detect only a premium of about 100 %, two to five times the premiums found elsewhere" vs :170 "The reading of the power, a detectable premium two to three times the published ones, is unchanged."
findings.problem: The article states the power-to-literature ratio two ways: "two to five times" in the opening section and "two to three times" under What changed. The second also claims the reading is "unchanged", but the benchmark changed (19–47 % now, 20–40 % as registered).
findings.evidence: An MDE of 100 % against 47 % is 2.1x, against 26 % 3.8x, and against Portugal's 19 % 5.3x, so "two to five" matches the body's 19–47 % range. Design §2 (corrected benchmark) says "two to three", which only fits "a third to a half". Design §5.4 still reads "2.5 times ... and 5 times".
findings.fix: Use one ratio in both places, e.g. "two to five times the published premiums (19–47 %)", or say that "two to three" refers to the Spain/Brazil/Italy band of a third to a half.
findings.note: Article line 99 says 'two to five times', line 206 says 'two to three times ... unchanged'. 100/47 = 2.1 and 100/19 = 5.3. Design §2 (line 204) says two to three and §5.4 (lines 382-383) says 2.5 and 5, so the registered reading did change.

findings.note: Design line 749 reads '### 30 September 2026, after an independent audit', and lines 183, 199, 549, 646 and 697 also say 30 Sep. git log -S puts that heading in ff0f0ca at 2026-09-29 05:18, and 9b3ce92 is dated 2026-09-29 02:14. The article says 29 September. Duplicate of [21].

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:69 "Studies of Spain[1], Brazil[2] and Italy[3] find that aligned municipalities receive roughly a third to a half more (about 40 %, 26–41 % and 36–47 %), ... in Germany ... +25 % under one and −20 to −40 % under the other[5]"
findings.problem: These magnitudes headline the deck, the meta description and the fig. 3 green band (26–47 %), but by the design's own statement they were never checked against the papers. The Brollo and Nannicini estimate is also narrower than the general premium the sentence implies.
findings.evidence: docs/research/prague-districts-design.md:202: "The magnitudes are taken from the audit and were not re-derived from the papers here." The Brollo and Nannicini abstract (OpenAlex, DOI 10.1017/S0003055412000433) says "in preelection years ... approximately one-third larger discretionary transfers for infrastructures". The Migueis abstract confirms 19 %. No abstract was available to confirm 36–47 % (Bracco), about 40 % (Solé-Ollé) or +25 / −20 to −40 % (Baskaran–Hessami).
findings.fix: Check each magnitude against the paper's tables and record the table or page in the design file. Qualify Brazil as "in pre-election years, infrastructure transfers". Until then, state that the figures are as reported by the audit.
findings.note: Design line 202: 'The magnitudes are taken from the audit and were not re-derived from the papers here.' The article presents them without qualification. I did not re-check the Brollo pre-election and infrastructure scope myself, but the admission that nothing was verified is enough to confirm.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:73 "the small districts on the edge spread from about 8 000 to 35 000, their figures driven by single projects"
findings.problem: The stated range leaves out the maximum among the small districts, and "on the edge" does not fit all of them.

Lysolaje is a small edge district at twice the stated top of the range. Praha 1, the centre, also falls in this group.
findings.fix: "the 44 smaller districts spread from about 7 800 to 35 500, and Praha-Lysolaje, after one large project, to 73 000", or say explicitly that Lysolaje is left out.
findings.note: districts.json, the 44 districts outside the largest 13: Zličín has the minimum, 7 763. The top is Lochkov 35 540, Praha 1 35 320 and Lysolaje 73 020. So 'about 8 000 to 35 000' leaves out Lysolaje, and Praha 1 (the centre) is in the group. Mitigation: the map caption does name Lysolaje as off the scale.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:165 "found an agreement of 0.72 (0.79 after the corrections below)"
findings.problem: The corrected bridge statistic is recorded as 0.795, which rounds to 0.80, not 0.79. No JSON holds the corrected value.

findings.fix: Write "0.80" (or "0.795"), and add the corrected value to prague-districts-bridge.json so it can be traced.
findings.note: Design line 799 gives 0.795, and the article writes 0.79. That is a rounding call that depends on unseen digits. The traceability gap is real: prague-districts-bridge.json holds only lin_ccc 0.7246, and grep found no corrected value in tools/praha or assets/praha. Low severity.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:93 "18 311 lines in all, with at least 98 % of the item lines read in every list"
findings.problem: The lowest coverage is 97.96 %, which is below 98 %, so "at least 98 %" is slightly overstated. The registered threshold was 97 %.
findings.evidence: docs/research/prague-districts-grants-structure.json: the 2019 drawdown 5.5 coverage is 0.9796 (the minimum). The design's Changes table gives 0.9796–0.9986. Parsed rows sum to 18 311 (this matches).
findings.fix: "at least 97.9 % of the item lines in every list (the registered rule was 97 %)".
findings.note: grants-structure.json: the minimum coverage is 0.9796 (2019, 5.5 drawdown), which is below 98 %. The 2015 5.3 coverage is None. Low severity.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:60 "MONITOR, Ministry of Finance, district reports 2015–2025" and :206 (r6) "budget reports (FIN 2-12 M) of each city district, 2015–2025"
findings.problem: The stated coverage says MONITOR supplies 2015–2025, but the district reports for 2015–2021 are empty. MONITOR is used only for 2022–2025, the window the table row "District side ... 2022–2025" gives.
findings.evidence: docs/research/prague-districts-design.md §0.4 "the empty 2015–2021 district reports" and §10 "MONITOR from 2022 only: accepted". Design §4.4 says MONITOR is used for 2022–2025.
findings.fix: Change both to "district reports 2022–2025 (earlier years are empty for the Prague districts)".
findings.note: Article line 89 and reference 6 say 'district reports 2015–2025'. Design §0.4 (line 76) says 'the empty 2015–2021 district reports', and line 517 says 'MONITOR from 2022 only: accepted'. The robustness row uses 2022–2025.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:198 "When the design was registered, the author had seen the descriptive budget figures of this page's first version ... and one 2025 grant total for one district, seen while the lists were parsed and outside every test window."
findings.problem: The disclosure of what was seen before registration is incomplete, and it is wrong to say that everything seen lay outside the test windows. The design file records that about 35 unmasked lines of the 2019 city-grant list were read before registration, with their amounts, for 12 districts. 2019 is year 0 of the 2018 event's post window, the year that gives that event its +70 %. The design also records city-wide 2025 totals from a header scan, and referees saw 2019 item-4137 figures for Praha 2 and 3. The single 2025 Praha 1 total that the article does mention was in fact seen after registration, not before.
findings.evidence: docs/research/prague-districts-design.md:83-93 (§0.4: '35 lines were read unmasked ... environmental grants ... each with its amount. The districts were Praha 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 17 and 18, Běchovice, ...'; 2025 city-wide sentences with amounts); :64-67 (§0.3 the data referee saw Praha 2/3 2019 4137); :677-679 (the 2025 Praha 1 row was seen during the post-registration parser step); assets/praha/districts_extended.json event_study.2018.by_year.2019 = 1.423 R (+70 %).
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "Before registration, the author had seen the descriptive 2022–2024 budget figures, about 35 lines of the 2019 grant list with their amounts (12 districts, inside the 2018 event's post window), city-wide 2025 totals, and, through the referees, two districts' 2019 transfer figures. One 2025 district total was seen later, while the lists were parsed. Full list: design §0."
findings.note: Design §0.4 lines 83-93: about 35 unmasked 2019 grant lines with amounts across 12 districts. 2019 is year 0 of the 2018 post window. The same section records city-wide 2025 totals, and §0.3 records referees seeing Praha 2 and 3 2019 item 4137. Line 677 places the 2025 Praha 1 total row inside the post-registration 29 Sep parser step. The article's sentence (line 198) omits these and wrongly says the one row was seen before registration and outside every window.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:136 "The effective sample is thus 30 switching districts in two events."
findings.problem: This overstates how much independent information the design has. The registered design says the treatment changes at party level, so the number of independent changes is the number of parties that switched: 4 entering parties over two events, and in 2023 essentially one party, ODS. The p-values come from district-level randomisation, which treats the 30 districts as independently assigned. The party-level permutation has only 20 possible sets. The article mentions the party problem later, but this sentence states the opposite.
findings.evidence: design.md:158-162 ('The number of independent treatment changes is the number of parties that switched: 4 entries and 4 exits'); :381 ('There are 30 switch-in units over two events, but only 4 entering parties'); districts_extended.json party_permutation.sets = 20.
findings.fix: "There are 30 switching districts, but they switched because four parties entered the city coalition, and in 2023 mainly one (ODS). The independent variation is therefore closer to four party changes than to 30 districts, and the district-level p-values should be read with that in mind."
findings.note: Article line 136: 'The effective sample is thus 30 switching districts in two events.' Design line 161 ('independent treatment changes is the number of parties that switched: 4 entries and 4 exits') and line 381 contradict it. party_permutation.sets = 20. Article line 163 discusses ODS but does not revise 'effective sample'.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:76 (tldr) "After the 2018 change, a modest premium is not ruled out." and :219 "the 2018 change alone points the other way (+20 %)"
findings.problem: The short version leads with a by-event subgroup result. It rests on 7 districts and on a single year, and the article gives no interval or test for it. Year 0 (2019) is +70 %, and years 1–2 are about 0 % and +19 %. The registered robustness check that drops the years next to each event was run, and it brings the 2018 estimate to −3 %. That check is not reported anywhere in the article. The 2018 event's own interval (Conley–Taber −23 % to +82 %, RI p = 0.16) is also not shown.
findings.evidence: assets/praha/districts_extended_robust.json checks.event_2018_only: relative 0.196, CT [-0.466, 1.672] R, p_ri 0.158, switch_in 7; checks.without_adjacent_years_2018_event_only: relative -0.026; design.md:480 registers 'dropping the regime-years adjacent to each event'; event_study.2018.by_year 2019 1.42, 2020 -0.007, 2021 0.39.
findings.fix: In the tldr: "The 2018 change alone gives +20 % (95 % CI about −23 to +82 %, 7 districts). That comes almost entirely from 2019, and it falls to about −3 % when the years next to the change are dropped." Add the dropped-adjacent-years check to the robustness table.
findings.note: The tldr sentence itself is defensible: event_2018_only gives a relative +19.6 % with CT −23 % to +82 %, so a modest premium is indeed not ruled out. What is confirmed is the omission. The registered §8.3 check without_adjacent_years_2018_event_only (relative −2.6 %) is in districts_extended_robust.json, but it is missing from the robustness table, which the article says 'gives the registered checks'. by_year 2019 = 1.42 R, which drives the +20 %.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:65 facts "smallest premium the design could detect ≈ 100 % at 80 % power · simulated before any grant was added up" (also deck :63 and :99)
findings.problem: The headline detectable effect overstates the power of the design that was actually run. The simulation assumed three years after the 2023 change (2023–2025). The bridge rule cut that to one year, so the real minimum detectable effect is larger than 100 %. The design file says the 100 % figure is 'optimistic'. The article mentions this only in the deviations list (:201), not next to the headline number. The simulation's own range across scenarios, 75–150 %, is also left out.
findings.evidence: design.md:450-452 (MDE 100 %, 75–150 % across scenarios); :725-727 ('The design-stage minimum detectable effect is therefore, if anything, optimistic for the realised design'); article :201.
findings.fix: Facts box: "≈ 100 % or more · simulated before any grant was added up for three post-years, 75–150 % across scenarios; the test as run has one post-year for 2023, so power is lower." Make the same change in the deck.
findings.note: Design lines 450-452 give an MDE of about 100 %, 75–150 % across scenarios. Lines 725-727 call it 'optimistic for the realised design'. The facts box and deck give 100 % without this caveat. It is disclosed only at line 201 (deviations) and line 219, so severity is moderate.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:124 "Money a district pays back to the city is left out, which covers loan repayments, returned grants and transfers"
findings.problem: The registered outcome rule counted returns as negative rows in the year of their resolution (§4.3). The primary outcome now leaves district-to-city flows out, and the registered version appears only as a robustness row (−36 %). The article presents this as a parser correction ('the parser counted money districts paid the city as grants', :203). It never says that the registered definition was changed. The effect is small, but the change itself is not disclosed.
findings.evidence: design.md:289 ('including returns (negative rows) in the year of their resolution'); :766-770 (district-to-city flows now 'excluded from the outcome'; sign-flip variant 'reported as robustness'); districts_extended_robust.json checks.signflip_district_to_city relative -0.362.
findings.fix: Add to the 'What changed' list: "The registered outcome counted returns as negative grants. After the flow-direction correction, returns are left out of the primary outcome, and the registered version is reported as a check (−36 %)."
findings.note: Design line 289 registered 'including returns (negative rows) in the year of their resolution', and lines 766-770 now exclude district-to-city flows. The registered version appears only as the robustness row '−36 %' and is not labelled as the registered definition. 'What changed' (line 203) frames it as a parser fix.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:270 changelog "Removed as descriptive and unregistered: ... the section on budget plans, capital spending and the 2024 formula"
findings.problem: These analyses were registered: H3 (capacity, exploratory), H4 (planned deficits, descriptive) and §7, the formula channel, which the design says 'is reported as a separate formula-level alignment channel'. All three were computed. The article drops them and calls them 'unregistered', and the 'What changed after registration' list does not say they were dropped. The 2024 formula change by alignment bears directly on the article's question. Unaligned districts got +18.8 % and aligned districts +12.3 %.
findings.evidence: design.md:167-171, 231-235 (H3, H4 registered outside the family); :468-474 (§7 formula channel 'reported'); assets/praha/districts_extended.json H3, H4 (gap_pc p=7.6e-9), formula_channel.2024_rule_change {0: 0.188, 1: 0.123}.
findings.fix: Either report H3, H4 and the 2024 formula change by alignment in one short paragraph, or add to 'What changed after registration': "The registered exploratory H3, the descriptive H4 and the formula channel (§7) were run but are not reported here. The results are in districts_extended.json." Then correct 'unregistered' in the change log.
findings.note: Design lines 167-171 register H3 and H4 outside the family, and lines 468-474 say §7 is 'reported'. districts_extended.json contains H3, H4 (gap_pc p = 7.6e-9) and formula_channel.2024_rule_change {0: 0.188, 1: 0.123}. Change log line 270 calls them 'unregistered'. Line 208 mentions only the four exploratory analyses that were not run.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:184 "Regression form of the same comparison −13 %"
findings.problem: A reader is told that the regression is 'the same comparison', yet it gives about a third of the headline estimate (−13 % against −37 %), and the article does not explain the gap. The stacked OLS with unit×event and year×event effects weights the two events by the variance of the treatment and by the number of years in each window. The headline estimate weights them by the number of switchers. Weighting is exactly what decides the sign here, because the two events have opposite signs.
findings.evidence: tools/praha/districts_extended.py:292-317 (unweighted OLS over the stacked rows; the 2018 stack has 6 years, the 2023 stack 4) against pooled() :256-267 (weights = switchers/total); districts_extended.json H1.regression.beta -0.227 vs H1.estimate -0.640.
findings.fix: Rename the row to "Regression form (OLS weights the two events differently)" and add in the note: "the regression gives the 2018 change more weight than the switcher-weighted headline, which is why it is less negative."
findings.note: pooled() weights events by switchers/total, while regression_form() fits unweighted stacked OLS with unit×event and yr×event dummies (tools/praha/districts_extended.py 256-317). beta −0.227 against estimate −0.640, and the article explains none of the gap.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:65, 74, 136, 149, 158, 161, 171, 173
findings.problem: Central technical terms are used before they are explained, or never explained. 'underpowered' and '80 % power' (:63, :65, :74) are never explained in plain words. 'controls' / 'controls' usual grants' (:66) is used before the control group is defined at :136. 'Holm thresholds' (:149) is not explained. 'joint pre-trend test' (:158) is not explained. 'Conley–Taber interval' (:161) is named only in a caption, while the body (:136) calls it 'a method for comparisons with few treated units' without the name, so the two cannot be linked. 'interregnum' (:171) is not explained. 'wild cluster bootstrap' and 'small-sample clustered errors' (:173) are not explained. The 'seat majority' and 'largest list' alignment rules (:170-171) are not explained until the robustness table.
findings.evidence: Read the full text in order. 'interregnum' is defined only in design.md:142-143. 'power' is first defined nowhere in the article.
findings.fix: Add short glosses at first use. For example, at :99: "underpowered (the test would usually miss a premium smaller than about 100 %)". At :136: "(Conley–Taber intervals)". At :149: "Holm thresholds, which correct for running two tests". At :158: "the pre-trend test (did the two groups already drift apart before the change?)". At :171: "the 2015–16 interregnum, when the city coalition had collapsed".
findings.note: Partly overstated. Conley–Taber is linked through footnote 14 at line 136, and 'underpowered' is glossed in the deck ('could detect about 100 %'). Still unexplained: 'joint pre-trend test', 'Holm thresholds', 'wild cluster bootstrap', 'small-sample clustered errors', 'interregnum' (fig. 4 caption) and '80 % power'.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:71-79 details.tldr
findings.problem: The short version gives no numbers and does not say what would overturn the result. It does not give the estimate and its interval, it does not compare the detectable effect (~100 %) with the published premiums (19–47 %), and it does not say that dropping one control district (Troja) or the ODS districts flips the sign. 'rests on a few districts' is too vague to act on. The most useful practical sentence, 'the results neither show a premium nor exclude one' (:214), appears only in the 'What this means' section near the end.
findings.evidence: tldr :74-78 compared with :214 and :188 (Troja ≈ 0 %), :187 (without ODS ≈ +14 %).
findings.fix: First bullet: "No premium was detected (−37 %, 95 % CI −115 to +21 %), but the test could only detect a premium of about 100 %, against 19–47 % elsewhere, so a typical premium may exist unseen." Second bullet: "The negative sign disappears without one control district (Troja) or without the districts with ODS mayors."
findings.note: Tldr lines 74-78 have no estimate, no interval and no MDE against the benchmark, and they do not mention the Troja or ODS sensitivity. 'Rests on a few districts' is vague. Low, editorial.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:99 "two to five times the premiums found elsewhere" vs :206 "The reading of the power, a detectable premium two to three times the published ones, is unchanged."
findings.problem: The article states the power reading in two inconsistent ways. The claim that it is 'unchanged' is also not accurate. As registered, it was 2.5 times the upper benchmark and 5 times the lower (design §5.4). Against 19–47 % it is about 2–5 times, and against 'a third to a half' it is 2–3 times.
findings.evidence: design.md:381-383 ('2.5 times the upper literature benchmark (40 %) and 5 times the lower (20 %)'); design.md:203-204 ('two to three times').
findings.fix: Use one reading throughout, for example "two to five times the published premiums (19–47 %)". In :206 write: "The registered reading was 2.5–5 times. Against the corrected benchmark it is about 2–5 times."
findings.note: Same as [1]. Lines 99 and 206 are inconsistent, and the registered reading in §5.4 was 2.5x and 5x, so 'unchanged' is inaccurate.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:158 "After the 2023 change ... −67 % against the three years before ... Pooled, the change on becoming aligned is −37 %"
findings.problem: Each event is scaled by its own controls' level: 2018 at +20 % of 2.03 R, 2023 at −67 % of 1.43 R. The pooled figure divides by the unweighted mean of the two levels. A reader who weights +20 % and −67 % by 7 and 23 switchers gets about −47 %, not −37 %, and the article does not say why the numbers differ.
findings.evidence: districts_extended.json H1.by_event (2018 pre_level_ctrl 2.029, 2023 1.435); H1.relative_to_control_pre_mean -0.370; design.md:707-708.
findings.fix: Add to the note under the tests table: "Per-event percentages are of each change's own controls. The pooled percentage is of their average, so it is not the weighted average of the two event percentages."
findings.note: by_event gives 0.398/2.029 = +19.6 % and −0.956/1.435 = −66.6 %. Switcher-weighted that is (7·19.6 + 23·(−66.6))/30 = −46.5 %. The pooled −0.640/1.732 = −37 % uses the unweighted mean of the levels (design 'Relative effect'). The article does not explain this.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:158 "Before each change the two groups moved similarly, and the joint pre-trend test gives p = 0.97."
findings.problem: The sentence reads a non-rejection from a low-power test as evidence of parallel trends. In 2017, before the 2018 change, the gap was +21 % of usual grants. That is the same size as the 2018 effect itself, and the article's HonestDiD bound is built on it.
findings.evidence: districts_extended.json event_study.2018.by_year.2017 = 0.422 R (+21 %); honest.max_pre_change 0.422.
findings.fix: "Before each change the gap between the groups stayed within about 20 % of usual grants (pre-trend test p = 0.97, a test with little power). The largest pre-change gap, +21 % in 2017, sets the HonestDiD bound in fig. 3."
findings.note: event_study.2018.by_year.2017 = 0.422 R, about +21 % of the 2.029 control level. honest.max_pre_change = 0.422. The article's 'moved similarly ... p = 0.97' reads a non-rejection as parallel trends. Low.

findings.location: texts/prague-districts.html:134 "Grants the outgoing, caretaker council decided in January and February 2023 count for the old coalition."
findings.problem: This is imprecise after the dating correction. Only grants up to 15 February count for the old coalition. The 112 rows (208 m CZK) approved on 16 February 2023, the day the new coalition took office, count for the new coalition and fall in the one-year 2023 post window.
findings.evidence: design.md:303-304 (1 Jan – 15 Feb 2023 belongs to r = 2022); :779 ('112 rows (208 m CZK) approved on 16 Feb 2023 move from regime-year 2022 to 2023').
findings.fix: "Grants decided by 15 February 2023 count for the old coalition. Those approved on 16 February 2023, the day the new coalition was elected (208 million crowns), count for the new one."
findings.note: Design lines 303-304 assign 1 Jan – 15 Feb 2023 to the old regime. Line 779 moves 112 rows (208 m CZK) approved on 16 Feb 2023 to regime-year 2023. So the article's 'January and February 2023' (line 134) is imprecise.

findings.location: docs/research/prague-districts-design.md:749 "### 30 September 2026, after an independent audit" (also :183, :199, :549) vs texts/prague-districts.html:198 "the changes below followed, all on 29 September 2026"
findings.problem: The design file dates the audit corrections to 30 September 2026. Git shows them committed on 29 September (9b3ce92 at 02:14, ff0f0ca at 05:18), which is what the article says. A reader who checks the dated deviations against the article finds two different dates.
findings.evidence: git show -s 9b3ce92: 2026-09-29 02:14:44; git log -S'30 September 2026, after an independent audit' -> ff0f0ca 2026-09-29 05:18:35.
findings.fix: Correct the design file's headings and inline notes to 29 September 2026, or explain the difference.
findings.note: Duplicate of [2]. The design file's headings and inline notes say 30 Sep 2026, but the only commits that carry that content are dated 29 Sep (9b3ce92 02:14 and ff0f0ca 05:18), matching the article.

findings.location: texts/prague-housing.html:11 (facts box) "+11.1 months · bootstrap 90 %: 8.7 to 12.6 · supported"
findings.problem: The headline facts card shows only the bootstrap percentile interval. The body text says this interval is too narrow and understates the uncertainty. The body puts the interval that matches the decision at a one-sided lower bound of 6.9 months, and the profile likelihood allows anything from about 6 (or 3) to more than 30 months. A reader of the card sees an uncertainty band the article itself rejects.
findings.evidence: Article lines 97–98 say the 5th–95th percentiles are 'narrower than that standard error implies' and that 'both bootstrap figures understate how uncertain Prague's own lag is'. housing_extended.json H2: se_boot 1.93, ci90 [8.72, 12.62]. The profile region runs from mu 14 to 38 (rel_loglik > −1.92), plus the isolated point at 11.
findings.fix: In the facts card, replace the interval with the decision-consistent figure, e.g. '+11.1 months · one-sided lower bound 6.9 at Holm's threshold; profile range about 6 to 30+ · supported'. Or add 'understates uncertainty' next to 8.7–12.6.
findings.note: Line 59 of the facts box shows only 'bootstrap 90 %: 8.7 to 12.6 · supported'. Lines 151-152 say this band is narrower than the SE implies and that both bootstrap figures understate the uncertainty, with a profile range of about 6 (3) to 30+. The JSON gives se_boot 1.93.

findings.location: texts/prague-housing.html:107 "In Warsaw the city built 96 homes that year and its public building societies none, 0.7 % of the year's 14 873" (also fig. 4 alt text line 104 '0.7 %')
findings.problem: Rounding error. 96 / 14 873 = 0.645 %, which rounds to 0.6 %. The 0.7 % comes from rounding the already rounded share 0.0065 a second time.
findings.evidence: cities.json: warsaw 2024 municipal 96, tbs 0, completed 14873; builders_2024.warsaw.municipal_and_tbs_share 0.0065. 96/14873 = 0.006455. The design §0 repeats 0.7 %.
findings.fix: Write '0.6 %' (or '0.65 %') in the text and the fig. 4 alt text. Also store the unrounded share in cities.json.
findings.note: 96/14873 = 0.00645, which is 0.6 %. cities.json stores municipal_and_tbs_share 0.0065. Line 162 text and the fig. 4 alt text (line 159) both say 0.7 %.

findings.location: texts/prague-housing.html:81 "on nearly the same definition across 22 countries, although Czechia, Spain and Croatia also count reconstructions"
findings.problem: Croatia is not among the 22 countries in the 208-region sample. Both its metro regions were dropped, so naming it as one of the sample countries that count reconstructions is inaccurate.
findings.evidence: Country count from housing_extended.json H1.plot: 22 countries (AT, BE, BG, CH, CY, CZ, DE, DK, EE, ES, FI, FR, HU, IT, LT, LU, NL, NO, PL, RO, SE, SK), with no HR. Design §5a drop table lists 'HR×2' (Census 2011 dwellings not traceable). The design's change log says 'Croatia had no region left in the sample'.
findings.fix: Change to 'although Czechia and Spain also count reconstructions (as does Croatia, whose regions dropped out of the sample)', or simply 'Czechia and Spain'.
findings.note: The H1.plot country set is 22 countries with no HR. Design line 470 drops HR×2, and the change log at line 927 says 'Croatia had no region left in the sample'. Line 134 still lists Croatia among the 22 that count reconstructions, and line 223 repeats it.

findings.location: texts/prague-housing.html:41 "The responsiveness of supply to prices has been estimated from national and metropolitan series<sup>5,6</sup>"
findings.problem: Neither cited source plausibly supports 'metropolitan series'. Caldera & Johansson (2013) estimate national OECD country series. Mayer & Somerville (2000a) use aggregate US national quarterly data. The metropolitan-level work in the design's literature list (Green, Malpezzi and Mayo 2005; Saiz 2010) is not cited here.
findings.evidence: Crossref metadata for 10.1016/j.jhe.2013.05.002 ('The price responsiveness of housing supply in OECD countries') and 10.1006/juec.1999.2158 match the references. The design §1 cites metro-level estimates separately (Green, Malpezzi & Mayo 2005; Saiz 2010).
findings.fix: Write 'from national series<sup>5,6</sup>', or add a metropolitan source such as Saiz (2010, QJE 125(3), 1253–1296) or Green, Malpezzi & Mayo (2005) if 'metropolitan' stays.
findings.note: r5 is Mayer & Somerville 2000, which uses US national aggregate series. r6 is Caldera & Johansson 2013, which uses OECD national series. Neither is metropolitan. Saiz 2010 and Green et al. 2005 appear in the design literature (lines 100, 799) but are not cited in the article.

findings.location: texts/prague-housing.html:203 ref r22 "Český statistický úřad (2025). Indices of realised flat prices by region, quarterly (icncr)."
findings.problem: The reference title appears to describe a different source from the one used. The design and referee report say icncr is a cadastre (ČÚZK purchase-contract) mean price per m² covering new and existing flats together. They treat 'ČSÚ realised existing-flat and new-flat indices' as a separate robustness source (3c), which was never downloaded. Calling icncr 'realised flat prices' merges it with that unused source.
findings.evidence: docs/research/prague-housing-design.md §3 'Prices (H3). icncr: ČÚZK cadastre purchase contracts, an unmixed mean price per m² of new and existing flats together' and §6 3c 'ČSÚ existing-flat and new-flat indices'. Change log: '3c (ČSÚ realised-price indices), not downloaded'. prague-housing-referees.md lines 24–31 say the same.
findings.fix: Retitle the reference, e.g. 'Price indices of flats from cadastre purchase contracts (ČÚZK data), by region, quarterly (icncr)'. In the note under the tests, say the index mixes new and existing flats.
findings.note: The downloaded xlsx (sheet 'ICN') holds kraj quarterly indices, but I could not extract its title. Purchase-contract prices from ČÚZK are realised prices, so 'realised flat prices' is not clearly wrong. The design (line 286) confirms that icncr mixes new and existing flats, and the article does not say so.

findings.location: texts/prague-housing.html:7 (deck), also meta description and ld+json: "a permitted flat in a new Prague apartment building takes about 11 months longer to be completed than elsewhere in Czechia"
findings.problem: The deck states the estimand as a per-flat completion time against all of Czechia. The registered estimand is a difference in mean distributed lags of aggregate monthly flows, against the 12 regions excluding Středočeský kraj. The body says it is 'not a clean difference in construction time' and that its size is weakly identified (about 6 to more than 30 months). The deck's wording is firmer than the result supports.
findings.evidence: Design RQ2: 'It is a property of the aggregate flow'; the reference group is the 12 kraje without Středočeský. Article line 99: 'a difference in the recorded pipeline ... and not a clean difference in construction time'.
findings.fix: E.g. 'finds that, in official monthly counts, completions of new Prague apartment buildings follow permits about 11 months later than in the rest of Czechia outside Středočeský kraj (supported), a gap of uncertain size that may partly reflect reporting timing.'
findings.note: The deck, meta and ld+json say 'takes about 11 months longer to be completed than elsewhere in Czechia'. The reference group excludes Středočeský (design and line 146). Line 153 says the figure is not a clean construction-time difference. The deck does add the reporting-timing caveat, which partly softens this. It overlaps with [7].

findings.location: assets/praha/housing_extended_robust.json addenda.date "2026-09-30" vs texts/prague-housing.html:151 and 224 ("29 September 2026, after the fact-check ... were added")
