findings.location: texts/prague-housing.html:55 and :59 (deck: "takes about 11 months longer to be completed"; facts: "+11.1 months · bootstrap 90 %: 8.7 to 12.6 · supported"); also :7 and :46 meta/ld description
findings.problem: The headline figures give the 11-month point estimate and the 8.7 to 12.6 bootstrap interval as the finding. At line 152 the article itself says both bootstrap figures understate the uncertainty: Prague's kernel is degenerate, the draws are warm-started from the estimate, and the profile likelihood puts the size anywhere from about 6 months (3 counting the isolated point) to more than 30. The deck, the facts box and the meta description show only the narrow interval, so the summary claims a precision that the body withdraws. The phrase "takes ... longer to be completed" also reads as construction time, which line 153 explicitly says it is not.
findings.evidence: housing_extended.json H2: phi_prague 17506 (degenerate), ci90 [8.72, 12.62], se_boot 1.93. tools/praha/housing_extended.py:305-306,364 shows bootstrap draws start at (f['mu'], f['phi']). Design 'Changes after registration' line 894-896: 'Prague's lag is weakly identified ... much wider than the bootstrap interval'. Article line 152: 'its size lies somewhere between about 6 months (3 ...) and more than 30 months'.
findings.fix: Deck: "A registered test finds that, in official monthly counts, completions of flats in new Prague apartment buildings follow permits with a longer recorded lag than elsewhere in Czechia (supported). The best fit is 11 months, but the data allow anything from about 6 to more than 30, and part of the gap may be reporting timing." findings.note: Deck line 55 and meta lines 7/46 give the per-flat 'takes longer to be completed' framing, and facts line 59 shows only the 8.7-12.6 bootstrap band. Body lines 152-153 and 216 withdraw both the precision and the construction-time reading. phi_prague is 17506, which is degenerate.

findings.location: texts/prague-housing.html:188 ("exponential lag; without the COVID months | a few bootstrap draws run off to unbounded lags; no information") and :201 ("The sign of the pipeline difference holds in every variant")
findings.problem: Changing only the kernel shape from gamma to exponential moves the point estimate from 11.1 to 40.6 months. The robustness table hides that point estimate behind "no information", so a reader cannot see that the size of the H2 gap depends heavily on the functional form. Only the bootstrap SE of that variant is uninformative; the point estimate is informative about model dependence.
findings.evidence: housing_extended_robust.json spec_curve.H2: d_exponential_kernel estimate 40.6 (p 0.50); e_without_covid_months 11.15; main 11.05; a_all_new_construction 4.97 (p 0.055).
findings.fix: In the table, show "+40.6 months (bootstrap diverged, no p)" for the exponential kernel and "+11.2 months (bootstrap diverged)" for the COVID exclusion. Add to line 201: "its size depends on the assumed lag shape: 11 months with the registered gamma kernel, 41 with an exponential one."
findings.note: spec_curve.H2: d_exponential_kernel has estimate 40.6 (p 0.5) and e_without_covid has 11.15. Table line 188 shows 'no information' with no estimates, and line 201 only claims that the sign holds.

findings.location: texts/prague-housing.html:114 ("expected the pipeline test to be decisive at a six-month difference unless monthly noise was as large as the signal")
findings.problem: Prague's realised noise-to-signal ratio was 3.3, well beyond the worst case simulated (1.0, where power at the SESOI was only 0.25 at α = 0.0167). The article states the design-stage power expectation in the methods but mentions the realised ratio only in the deviation list (line 208), not near the H2 result. A test that passes under far lower power than planned is more likely to exaggerate the size of the effect, and that bears directly on the 11-month figure.
findings.evidence: housing_extended.json H2.noise_ratio.prague 3.29, underpowered_rule_triggered True; design §5a power table: noise ratio 1.0 gives power 0.25 (0.39) at Δμ = 6.
findings.fix: Add to the H2 section after line 151: "Prague's monthly noise turned out to be 3.3 times the fitted signal, more than the design's power simulations covered (at a ratio of 1, power at a 6-month difference was only 25 %), so the size of a passing estimate may be exaggerated."
findings.note: noise_ratio.prague is 3.29. The design power table tops out at a ratio of 1.0, with power 0.25 at Δμ=6 and α=0.0167. The article reports 3.3 only in the deviation list (line 208) and does not say the realised ratio is outside the simulated range, or what that implies for the size of a passing estimate.

findings.location: texts/prague-housing.html:152 ("In the bootstrap the completion yield and the lag are almost uncorrelated (−0.05)")
findings.problem: The fitted yield θ is never reported, although it is very different between the two units: 0.26 in Prague and 0.72 in the rest. In other words, the model links only about a quarter of Prague's permitted flats to completions. That bears on whether the Prague lag is estimated from a real signal, and on the composition and reporting reading. "Completion yield" is also used without being defined.
findings.evidence: housing_extended.json H2: theta_prague 0.255, theta_rest 0.719; design RQ2 says never-built projects lower θ.
findings.fix: After line 151 add: "The model also estimates what share of permitted flats turns into completions: about a quarter in Prague against about 70 % elsewhere, so Prague's lag rests on a weak link between the two series." Define the yield at first use.
findings.note: theta_prague is 0.255 and theta_rest 0.719 in housing_extended.json. Neither is reported anywhere in the article. 'Completion yield' first appears at line 152 with no definition.

findings.location: texts/prague-housing.html:58 (facts: "5.28 ... 163rd of 208, median 3.55") and :135 ("which places it 163rd of 208 from the bottom, in Europe's upper quarter"); TLDR :66 ("its region builds more than most")

On the comparable ČSÚ count of new houses, Prague's region builds 3.88 against a median of 3.50 and ranks 116th of 208, which is mid-table. The headline card shows only the inflated figure.

findings.fix: Facts box: "5.28 by the census count, which in Czechia includes reconstructions (163rd of 208); 3.88 counting new houses only (116th, median 3.50)". Line 135: replace "in Europe's upper quarter" with "in the upper quarter on this count, which includes Czech reconstructions; mid-table on new houses alone".

The facts box (line 58), however, shows only 5.28 and 163rd, with no reconstruction caveat. The TLDR line 'builds more than most' still holds at 116/208, so that part is not wrong.

findings.location: texts/prague-housing.html:60 (facts: "−0.23 ... 90 % Conley: −0.349 to −0.105 · indeterminate") and :217
findings.problem: The only interval shown for H5, in both the facts box and the summary, is the Conley interval, which excludes zero. The label next to it is "indeterminate". The decisive p-value (the district wild bootstrap, 0.0252, about 14 effective clusters) is not shown there, so the reader sees an interval clear of zero beside a non-result. The robustness table rendered by JS will also print H5 as "robust: yes" (87.5 % of specifications at p < 0.05), and the prose does not reconcile that with "indeterminate".
findings.evidence: housing_extended.json H5: ci90_conley [-0.349,-0.105], p_conley 0.0011, p_wcr 0.0252, effective_clusters 13.7; housing_extended_robust.json spec_curve.H5 robust True, share_p_below_005 0.875.
findings.fix: Facts box: "−0.23 · decision p 0.0252 against 0.025 (district bootstrap, ~14 clusters) · indeterminate". Below the spec-curve table add: "'Robust' uses unadjusted p < 0.05; H5 still missed its Holm threshold."

The decisive p_wcr of 0.0252 is given only in the table and at line 177. spec_curve.H5 has robust true with share_p_below_005 0.875, and the prose does not reconcile this with the indeterminate label.

findings.location: texts/prague-housing.html:63-70 (details.tldr)
findings.problem: The short version does not give the size of the one supported result or what it rests on (one treated unit, monthly regional aggregates, a weakly identified lag). It also does not say what would overturn it, for example a different lag shape or evidence on reporting timing. Bullet 2 uses the undefined term "pipeline gap". The most useful practical sentence is buried at lines 153 and 216: the result excludes the time needed to obtain a permit, which is the step Czech reform targeted. Without it, a reader can take the gap as evidence that permitting is slow. Bullet 4 also calls H1 and H3 "tests", but the design demoted them to estimates.
findings.evidence: Lines 66-69 compared with lines 152-153 and 216; design §2 says H1 and H3 are 'Estimates with pre-written reporting rules'.
findings.fix: Replace bullets 2-3 with: "After a permit, Prague's flats in new apartment buildings take longer to be recorded as completed than elsewhere in Czechia: best fit 11 months, plausibly 6 to 30+. This is the one registered test that passed. It does not cover how long getting the permit takes, and part of it may be when completions are registered or project size. A different lag model gives a much larger gap (41 months), so the size is uncertain; the direction is not." Bullet 4: "the demand and price estimates and the Polish builders' test are uninformative."
findings.note: The TLDR (lines 66-69) gives no size or range for H2. 'Pipeline gap' is undefined. It omits that the gap excludes permit time. Bullet 4 calls the H1/H3 estimates 'tests' (the demand and price tests), but line 113 says they were demoted to estimates.

findings.problem: Central technical terms are used without a plain explanation at first use: "family-wise error rate" and "Holm's procedure" (113); μP − μR, βNM − βM and γ (122-124, symbols never defined in words); "conformal rank" (125); "EWC" (126, expanded only at 129); "stationary block bootstrap" and "wild score bootstrap" (129); "log points" (129); "studentised leave-one-country-out scores" (139); "one-sided lower bound at Holm's threshold" (151); "degenerate" fitted lag distribution and "completion yield" (152); "common support" (163); "specification curve" (197); and "log density" and "Conley" in the facts box (60) before any explanation.
findings.evidence: A read of the lines cited; none carries a glossary or tooltip, and line 136 is the only place that paraphrases a method in plain words.
findings.fix: Add a one-clause gloss at first use, e.g. "Holm's procedure, which tightens the p-value threshold so that three tests together have at most a 5 % chance of any false positive"; "degenerate: the model puts every flat at exactly 16 months, with no spread"; "specification curve: the same test rerun under each registered variant"; and write the table symbols as "Prague's mean lag minus the rest's", etc.
findings.note: Line 126 uses 'EWC' before it is expanded at line 129. The symbols μP−μR, βNM−βM and γ, and the terms conformal rank, Holm, FWER, 'degenerate', 'completion yield', 'common support' and 'specification curve', appear with no plain gloss. The facts box line 60 uses 'Conley' and 'log density' before any explanation.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html, New cars in the register: "that route gives 10.4 cm, while the published European ratio of 0.618 would turn the same wheelbase into 13.0 cm"
findings.problem: The two figures do not come from the same wheelbase change. 10.4 cm is the registered trend slope (7.07 mm a year x 10 = 70.7 mm) x b-hat 1.474. 13.0 cm is the endpoint change (+80.2 mm) / 0.618, taken from Part II's pipeline. Applied to the same 70.7 mm slope, the 0.618 ratio gives 11.4 cm. The sentence attributes the whole 2.6 cm difference to the choice of ratio, but only about 1.0 cm of it comes from the ratio.
findings.evidence: assets/parking6/h2.json: comparator_C_cm 10.424, b_hat 1.474, eea_slope_mm_per_year 7.072. assets/parking6/part2_correction.json m1_m1g: wheelbase_change_mm 80.16, length_change central 12.97. docs/research/prague-parking-ds.json eea_m1g: endpoints 80.2 mm, trend 70.7 mm per decade. 70.72/0.618 = 114.4 mm; 80.16/0.618 = 129.7 mm.
findings.fix: Either compare on the same basis ("the published European ratio of 0.618 would turn the same wheelbase trend into 11.4 cm") or say that 13.0 cm is the endpoint change from Part II's corrected pipeline.
findings.note: In h2.json, comparator_C_cm 10.424 = eea_slope 7.072 mm/yr x 10 x b_hat 1.474, which is the trend basis. In part2_correction.json, wheelbase_change_mm is 80.16 and length central is 12.97, so 80.16/0.618 = 129.7 mm on the endpoint basis. Putting the same 70.7 mm through /0.618 gives 11.4 cm. The sentence therefore compares two different bases.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html, The question: "a change Transport & Environment (T&E) has measured for the hundred best-selling models in the EU[1]"; r1: "Dimension series for the 100 best-selling EU models"
findings.problem: The cited 2026 T&E report (Ever-bigger?) does not describe its dimension series as the 100 best-selling EU models. The annex table is 'Average dimensions of new sales', the scope is 'EU, UK & Norway', and the data come from Inovev. The 'top-100' description looks carried over from an earlier T&E source that this article does not cite.
findings.evidence: Downloaded the r1 PDF and ran pdftotext. No 'best-selling', 'top 100' or 'hundred' appears anywhere in it. The text says 'Scope is EU, UK & Norway', the annex p.26 table is headed 'Average dimensions of new sales' (2025: 4.38 m length, 1.82 m width), and it refers to 'Inovev vehicle dimension data'.
findings.fix: Describe the source as T&E's series of average dimensions of new cars sold in the EU, UK and Norway, or cite the T&E publication that actually uses the top-100 models.
findings.note: I downloaded the r1 PDF and ran pdftotext. It contains no 'best-selling', 'top 100' or 'hundred'. Its wording is 'Scope is EU, UK & Norway' and the annex table is headed 'Average dimensions of new sales'. The design file (line 25) calls Part I's source 'T&E EU top-100 new-car series', which suggests the description was carried over from an older source.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html, How this was done: "g = 0.82 m ... the gap of 0.82 m is the difference between T&E's end-to-end pitch of 5.20 m ... and its average car of 4.38 m[1]"
findings.problem: This misstates both the source and the model. (a) T&E derives its manoeuvring space from the fleet-average length in 2025. 4.38 m is T&E's new-sales average, so 5.20 - 4.38 is not T&E's gap. (b) The registered model, and the code as run, do not use a fixed 0.82 m. They draw g = p - L2025 (register fleet) with p ~ triangular(4.9, 5.2, 5.5), which gives a median g of 0.83 m and a range of 0.59-1.06 m.
findings.evidence: T&E PDF annex, Parking analysis (1/2): 'Required manoeuvring space derived from the relationship between average fleet length in 2025 and end-to-end car parking space length'. 4.38 m is in the 'new sales' table. docs/research/prague-parking-design.md:328 'In each draw g = p − L̄₂₀₂₅'. assets/parking6/e1.json g: q025 0.593, median 0.829, q975 1.065.
findings.fix: State g as the registered one: g = p − L̄₂₀₂₅, with p drawn around T&E's 5.20 m pitch, central g ≈ 0.83 m (0.59–1.06 m). Drop the attribution of 4.38 m as the car length T&E used for the gap.
findings.note: The T&E annex says 'Required manoeuvring space derived from the relationship between average fleet length in 2025 and end-to-end car parking space length', and 4.38 is the new-sales figure. The code draws g = p - L25 with p ~ triangular(4.9, 5.2, 5.5). In e1.json, g has median 0.829 and range 0.593-1.065. The article's fixed g = 0.82 m and its attribution to 4.38 are both wrong.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:71, metadata: "published 14 September 2026 (first estimate; ...)" vs r6: "(Text 01), 8 September 2026"

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html, r17: "Holder, D. et al. (2021). Systematic analysis of changing vehicle exterior dimensions. Proceedings of the Design Society 1 (ICED21)."
findings.problem: The authors, title and pages are wrong or missing. Crossref and the publisher page list one author only, Daniel Holder, so 'et al.' is wrong. The title is cut short (the full title ends 'and relevant vehicle proportions'), and the pages (2921–2930) are missing.

Design Society vol. 1, pp. 2921–2930, 2021. The Cambridge page has a single citation_author, 'Daniel Holder'.
findings.fix: Holder, D. (2021). Systematic analysis of changing vehicle exterior dimensions and relevant vehicle proportions. Proceedings of the Design Society 1, 2921–2930. doi:10.1017/pds.2021.553.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html, Reproduction, steps 6–7: "part2_m1g.py, the wheelbase-route comparator; parking6_estimate.py, the tests and estimates, written to assets/parking6/h2.json..."

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html, What today's kerb would hold: "Per parallel space, 2.7 % ... is far below T&E's headline pro-rated ... (7.4–12.1 %) and close to what T&E's own parameters imply (2.9–3.4 %)"
findings.problem: This does not follow the reporting sentence the plan fixed in advance. findings.evidence: docs/research/prague-parking-design.md:185-188. assets/parking6/e1.json theta_u median 0.02695; te_comparison part1_reproduction_prorated_pct [2.9, 3.4].

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:99, map caption: "summed into 547 cells of a 450 m grid ...; the one cell in Praha 16 (Radotín, 18 stalls) ... is left off"
findings.problem: The 547 cells are the cells drawn on the map, without Praha 16. With the Praha 16 cell the grid has 548 cells. As written, the caption reads as if the left-off cell were one of the 547.
findings.evidence: assets/parking6/map-zones.json: 547 features, stalls summing to 168 406 (= 168 424 − 18) and 16 873 segments. No feature is named Praha 16.
findings.fix: "summed into 548 cells of a 450 m grid ...; the one cell in Praha 16 (Radotín, 18 stalls), 4 km south of the rest, is left off, so the map shows 547."
findings.note: map-zones.json has 547 features, with the note 'Left off the map: Praha 16, 18 stalls'. 547 therefore excludes the Praha 16 cell, while the caption says all segments were summed into 547 cells and then one was left off.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html, New cars in the register: "T&E's figures are rounded to the centimetre, which moves a three-year difference by up to about 0.7 cm"
findings.problem: The 6.0 cm comes from T&E's 2020 and 2025 values (2022 is interpolated). The difference is 0.6 x (L2025 − L2020), so centimetre rounding moves it by at most 0.6 cm. If both 3-year endpoints were rounded independently the bound would be 1.0 cm. Neither bound is 0.7. The figure was carried over from the design without a derivation.
findings.evidence: T&E table: 2020 4.28 m, 2025 4.38 m. The design (line 153) gives 2022 = 4.32 'by interpolation'. assets/parking6/h2.json te_rounding_note_cm 0.7, hard-coded.
findings.fix: Give the derived bound ('by up to about 0.6 cm') or state how 0.7 cm was obtained.
findings.note: T&E gives 2020 = 4.28 and 2025 = 4.38, with 2022 interpolated, so Δ = 0.6(L25 - L20). Centimetre rounding (±0.5 each) bounds Δ at ±0.6 cm. The 0.7 is hard-coded in h2.json and in design line 158, with no derivation.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:63 (tldr) "The estimate treats every parallel bay as unmarked, so it is an upper bound."; also :157 and :236
findings.problem: 'Upper bound' is stated without qualification, but 1.6 % is only an upper bound with respect to bay marking. Under the registered structural alternative (gap proportional to length, design §4 'Gap (E.1)', reported as a second estimate) the loss is larger: θ₁ᵘ = 3.2 % (2.6–3.8) against 2.7 %, which puts θ₁ at about 1.9 %. The 3.9 cm calibration shortfall also has an unknown direction of effect. The summary box tells readers the true figure is at most 1.6 %, which the analysis does not support.
findings.evidence: assets/parking6/e1.json theta_u_prop median 0.0321 (0.0260–0.0383) vs theta_u 0.0270. With s = 0.59, θ₁ = s(ρ−1)/(1+s(ρ−1)) ≈ 0.019 at θᵘ = 0.032 (parking6_estimate.py:373). Design §4 lists the proportional gap as one of two reported structural estimates.
findings.fix: In the tldr and at :157: "Because every parallel bay is treated as unmarked, painted bays could only lower the estimate (to 1.0–1.3 % if a quarter to half are painted). Under the plan's other gap rule (gap proportional to length) it would be higher, about 1.9 %." Also report θ₁ under the proportional gap in the estimates table, not only θ₁ᵘ in Robustness.
findings.note: Design line 330 registers a proportional gap as the second structural estimate, and T&E's own method also assumes a proportional gap. In e1.json, theta_u_prop median is 0.0321 (0.026-0.038) against 0.0270. With s = 0.59 that gives θ₁ ≈ 1.9 %. 'Upper bound' holds only for the painted-bay dimension, yet the tldr and line 236 state it without qualification.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:55 facts "+2.3 cm … 95 % CI −0.3 to +5.2"; :7 meta "New cars in Czechia grew 2.3 cm in 2022–2025"; :131 "New cars grew by 2.3 cm over those three years"
findings.problem: The interval includes zero, yet the description, deck and body all state 'grew 2.3 cm' as a finding. The registered test only shows growth below 6.0 cm. It does not show that cars grew at all.
findings.evidence: h2.json tests.ci95_delta2 = [−0.27, 5.17]. The test is one-sided against 6.0 (p_h2b 0.0072).
findings.fix: "New cars in Czechia changed by +2.3 cm over 2022–2025 (95 % CI −0.3 to +5.2): less than T&E's 6.0 cm, though the data cannot rule out no growth at all." Use the same wording in the meta description and og text.
findings.note: h2.json ci95_delta2 = [-0.27, 5.17], so the interval includes zero. The JSON-LD/meta description says 'New cars in Czechia grew 2.3 cm in 2022–2025' with no interval. The body gives the CI but never says that no growth cannot be ruled out.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:193 "For every input, the plan asked how far it would have to move … No single input can do so"; :215-230 change lists
findings.problem: Several registered robustness checks were not run or not reported, and the 'Not done' bullet (:229) omits them. These are R4 (discrete segment model), R5 (N1 included, used imports excluded, STK-active age scaling, Prague fleet), R6 (exponential/uniform survival), R10 (area model), R13 (specification curve), R12 (H2 sensitivity) and the registered leave-one-model-out listing. R12 and LOMO were computed but not reported. Dropping the largest model line (Octavia) moves the H2a difference from 2.3 to 4.2 cm, close to the ±4.4 cm margin, and endpoint means give 4.0 cm.
findings.evidence: h2.json r12: drop_largest_line d_cm 4.16, endpoints d_cm 3.98, unweighted 1.78. lomo_top lists the Octavia at a weight of 0.099. Design §2.1 'Both: Leave-one-model-out influence, with the largest listed' and §6 R1–R13. grep of parking6_estimate.py finds no N1, exponential, discrete or specification-curve code.
findings.fix: Extend the 'Not done' bullet: "the registered robustness checks R4, R5, R6, R10 and R13 were not run." Add one sentence under the tests: "Leaving out the Octavia (10 % of weight) moves the H2a difference to 4.2 cm and endpoint means give 4.0 cm; H2b stays at 2.2–2.7 cm in all registered sensitivity runs."
findings.note: Design §6 lists R4, R5, R6, R10 and R13, and grep of tools/parking6 finds no code for N1-in-fleet, exponential/uniform survival, a discrete segment model or a specification curve. The article's 'Not done' bullet omits them. h2.json r12 has drop_largest_line d_cm 4.16 and endpoints 3.98, and lomo_top lists the Octavia at 0.099. Neither is reported, although design line 160 requires the LOMO listing.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:64 (tldr) "Almost all of the uncertainty comes from the lengths of cars made before 2010."; :209 "(a first-order share of 0.92 …)"
findings.problem: The 0.92 share applies only to the uncertainty the Monte Carlo puts in. The parallel share's interval (58–60 %) reflects only binomial noise in the 2019 PPV/NPV, from four districts. It includes no transfer error to the whole city in 2026 (the registered 2026 orthophoto validation was not done), so its Sobol share comes out at about 0. Other unquantified sources are also outside the range: the 3.9 cm calibration failure and the national-versus-parked fleet. Presenting 'almost all of the uncertainty' in the summary overstates how complete the range is.
findings.evidence: parking6_estimate.py:355,371: s depends only on Beta(PPV/NPV) draws. e1.json s 0.582–0.601 and sobol parallel_share −0.015. θ₁ scales almost linearly with s (tipping s 0.85 → 2.30 %). Design change log: 'No 2026 orthophoto validation sample'.
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Within the registered input ranges, almost all of the spread comes from the lengths of pre-2010 cars. The range does not include error in the parallel share (validated only on 2019 labels in Prague 4, 5, 6 and 9), the 3.9 cm calibration gap, or the difference between the national fleet and the cars parked in Prague."
findings.note: Code line ~371: s varies only through the Beta(PPV/NPV) draws. e1.json gives s 0.582-0.601 and a Sobol parallel_share of -0.015, but the tipping point shows θ₁ is highly sensitive to s (0.85 gives 2.30 %). The 0.92 share applies only within the modelled inputs, so the tldr's unqualified 'almost all of the uncertainty' overstates it.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:236 "What this means" and :54/:139-151 main result; the calibration failure appears only at :210 and :241
findings.problem: The registered calibration check failed: the modelled 2025 fleet is 3.9 cm shorter than the measured one. That is about 28 % of the modelled 2012→2025 fleet growth of 14 cm, which drives θ₁. The failure appears only in Robustness and in the closing limitations, not next to the headline or in the tldr.
findings.evidence: e1.json calibration_2025: measured 4.408, modelled 4.370, diff 3.89 cm. L12 4.229 → L25 4.370 (14.0 cm).
findings.fix: Add one sentence after the estimates table at :149: "The fleet model fails its registered calibration check, with the modelled 2025 fleet 3.9 cm shorter than the register's, about a quarter of the 14 cm growth that drives this estimate. If that error differs between 2012 and 2025, the estimate moves accordingly." Add a short version to the tldr.
findings.note: e1.json calibration_2025 diff is 3.89 cm, against L12 → L25 of 4.229 → 4.370 (14.0 cm), i.e. about 28 %. The article mentions the failure only in Robustness, in 'What changed' and in 'What this does not show', not next to the estimates table or in the tldr.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:60-69 details.tldr
findings.problem: The short-version box states neither result. It has no 1.6 % (1.3–1.9), no ~2 800 stalls, no H2b result (+2.3 cm vs 6.0) and no 120 Kč. Its third bullet, 'The other registered test was inconclusive', refers to a test the box never introduced. It does not say what the result rests on (the modelled 2012 fleet, the shape-read parallel share, the national rather than Prague fleet) or what would overturn it (the parallel share reaching ≥ 93 %, or a different gap law). The most practical sentence, that a length-priced permit would change prices by only ~120 Kč a year and by more than 10 % for only 2 % of cars, appears only at :168.
findings.evidence: Lines 62-68 contain no numbers except none. The practical figures are at :168 and :236.
findings.fix: Lead with "Today's paid kerb would hold about 1.6 % (1.3–1.9 %) more cars, about 2 800 stalls, if they were 2012's cars; per parallel space 2.7 %." Then: "New Czech cars grew less over 2022–2025 than T&E's series implies (+2.3 cm, CI −0.3 to +5.2, vs 6.0; registered test passed). The second test, agreement with the wheelbase route, was inconclusive." Then: "It rests on a modelled 2012 fleet and a parallel share read from segment shape; only a parallel share above about 93 % would move it out of its band." Then: "A permit priced by length would separate a long and a short car by about 120 Kč a year."
findings.note: The tldr bullets (stripped lines 23-27) contain no numbers. 'The other registered test was inconclusive' refers to a test the box never introduced. The 120 Kč and 2 % figures appear only in the body.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:236 "The central quantity is θ₁"; :144-145 estimates table
findings.problem: The design (§1 RQ1) names θ₁ᵘ, the per-parallel-space loss, as the 'Primary' estimand. It also says 'θ₁ in per cent is the headline'. The article leads with θ₁, which falls inside one band, and never says the registered primary was θ₁ᵘ, which straddles two bands (2.2–3.2 %). The design also says E1's band was 'very likely known in advance', so E1 is descriptive by rule A.4. The article does not tell readers that the band result was predictable before the run.
findings.evidence: Design §1 "Primary: θ₁ᵘ, the loss on unmarked parallel kerb" and "θ₁ in per cent is the headline". Design §2.2: "The band is therefore very likely known in advance, and E1 is descriptive by rule A.4." e1.json band_theta_u "straddles".
findings.fix: At :105 or :150 add: "The plan named the per-parallel-space loss θ₁ᵘ as its primary estimand and the all-stalls share θ₁ as the headline. Since the earlier texts had already put θ₁ near 1.6 %, its band was expected in advance, and the estimate is descriptive rather than a test."
findings.note: Design line 111 says 'Primary: θ₁ᵘ' and line 120 says 'θ₁ in per cent is the headline'. Line 190 says the band is 'very likely known in advance... E1 is descriptive by rule A.4'. The article says 'The central quantity is θ₁' and never names θ₁ᵘ as the primary estimand or mentions that the band was predictable. It does say estimates are 'reported rather than tested'.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:94 "model line"; :105 "family-wise error rate", "Holm's procedure", "bands"; :109 "studentised bootstrap clustered by model line", "survival curve"; :117 "equivalence within ±4.4 cm"; :144-147 "θ₁", "θ₁ᵘ"
findings.problem: Central technical terms appear without explanation at first use. 'Model line' (the cluster unit of both tests, defined only in design §3 as the first token of the commercial name) is never defined. θ₁ and θ₁ᵘ first appear as table labels with no definition of θ₁ as a share of the 2012-fleet capacity. The 'bands' at :105 are explained only at :150. 'Equivalence test' (TOST) is not explained, which matters because the result hinges on it. 'Studentised bootstrap clustered by model line' and 'family-wise error rate' are unexplained for general readers.
findings.evidence: First uses at the lines cited. No inline gloss. The line key definition exists only in the design change log ('first token of the commercial name').
findings.fix: At :94: "a model line (make plus the first word of the model name, e.g. Škoda Octavia)". At :105: "bands (ranges such as 1–2.5 %, each with a sentence written in advance)". At :117: "an equivalence test, which asks whether the difference is shown to lie inside ±4.4 cm". Before the table at :140: "θ₁ is the extra cars as a share of all stalls; θ₁ᵘ the same per space on unmarked parallel kerb."
findings.note: 'Model line' is never defined in the article. θ₁ and θ₁ᵘ first appear as table labels. TOST and 'family-wise error rate' are not glossed. This is a clarity point, but the gaps are real.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:201 "shape of the survival curve | k 1.4 – 1.6"; :209 "first-order share of 0.92 in a variance decomposition"; :219 "imputation variance", "inner bootstrap of 50 draws", "reduced size check"; :225 "size check … rejected at 0.11"; :228 "revenue-neutral"; :95 "S-JTSK"
findings.problem: Secondary terms are unexplained. 'k' is introduced with no mention that the survival curve is Weibull or what k controls. 'First-order share', 'size check', 'inner bootstrap' and 'revenue-neutral' are not glossed. :225 does not say that a size-check rate of 0.11 means the H2a lower-tail test may be liberal.
findings.evidence: No definitions at or before the cited lines.
findings.fix: Gloss inline. "k, which sets how sharply scrappage rises with age (Weibull shape)"; "a size check (how often the test wrongly rejects when the null is exactly true; 0.11 against 0.05 means it may be too liberal)"; "revenue-neutral (the average permit stays at 1 200 Kč)"; "S-JTSK, the Czech national grid".
findings.note: k is labelled only 'shape of the survival curve', with no mention of Weibull. 'Size check... rejected at 0.11', 'inner bootstrap', 'first-order share' and 'revenue-neutral' are unexplained, and the text does not say that 0.11 implies a liberal test. Low severity.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:162 "about 5.2 m of kerb for the register's average parked car of 4.37 m"
findings.problem: 4.37 m is the modelled 2025 fleet mean, not the register's measured value. The register's national active fleet averages 4.41 m (the 3.9 cm calibration gap). It is also not a 'parked' car: the article itself says the parked mix is unknown.
findings.evidence: e1.json L25 median 4.370 (modelled). calibration_2025 measured_active_m 4.408. e4.json L_mean_m 4.414.
findings.fix: "about 5.2 m of kerb for the modelled average car of the 2025 fleet, 4.37 m (4.41 m in the register's cars in operation)"
findings.note: 4.37 is e1.json L25 median 4.3697, which is modelled. The register's measured active fleet is 4.408 (calibration_2025) and e4 L_mean is 4.414. Calling it the 'register's average parked car' is inaccurate on both counts.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:193 "against the 58–60 % measured"; :96 "puts 59 % of stalls on parallel kerb"
findings.problem: The parallel share is not measured. It is inferred from segment shape and corrected with PPV/NPV from 2019 labels in four districts. Only that ground truth gave a true parallel share of 0.70. Calling 58–60 % 'measured' and giving it a tight range gives the tipping-point argument (93 % needed) more certainty than it has.
findings.evidence: Design §5 DS4: '2019 true parallel share (0.70, stall-weighted) covers P4, P5, P6 and P9 only… not used as s'. parking6_estimate.py:371.
findings.fix: "against the 58–60 % estimated from segment shape (an interval that reflects only the 2019 classifier's error rates, not a 2026 check)"
findings.note: Robustness line 89 says 'against the 58–60 % measured'. s is a PPV/NPV-corrected classifier estimate whose interval comes only from Beta draws on the 2019 P4/5/6/9 labels (design line 385: the true share 0.70 there is not representative). Calling it 'measured' overstates it.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:126 "1.47 mm of length per mm of wheelbase, … while the published European ratio of 0.618"
findings.problem: The two ratios run in opposite directions: 1.47 is length per wheelbase, and 0.618 is wheelbase per length (1/0.618 = 1.62). Set side by side, they read as if 0.618 were the smaller conversion.
findings.evidence: Reference 17: 'Wheelbase/length 0.618'. b_hat 1.474 in h2.json.
findings.fix: "… 1.47 mm of length per mm of wheelbase, while the published European ratio (wheelbase 0.618 of length, i.e. 1.62 mm of length per mm) would turn the same wheelbase into 13.0 cm."
findings.note: Reference 17 gives 'Wheelbase/length 0.618' while b_hat 1.474 is length per wheelbase. The two are set side by side with no note on direction. Minor clarity issue.

findings.location: texts/prague-parking.html:151 "Which of the two holds depends above all on how long the cars made before 2010 really were (fig. 5)"
findings.problem: Fig. 5 and the Robustness table show tipping points for θ₁ (all stalls), not for θ₁ᵘ, the estimate that straddles the bands. The registered gap-law switch, not shown in fig. 5, would by itself put θ₁ᵘ wholly in the 2.5–5 % band (2.6–3.8 %).
findings.evidence: e1.json tipping is computed on 'theta' only. theta_u_prop 0.026–0.038.
findings.fix: "Which holds depends mainly on the pre-2010 lengths and on the gap rule: with a gap proportional to length, the per-space loss sits wholly in 2.5–5 % (2.6–3.8 %)."
findings.note: e1.json tipping is computed on θ (all stalls) only, and fig. 5 shows θ₁, yet the sentence about θ₁ᵘ straddling the bands points to fig. 5. theta_u_prop 2.6-3.8 % lies wholly in the 2.5-5 band, so the gap rule also decides between the bands.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:121 "(H2 supported; bootstrap 90 % interval 8.7 to 12.6)"
findings.problem: The hub gives the 5th to 95th bootstrap percentiles as the uncertainty on the 11-month pipeline gap and adds no caveat. The registered design's post-estimation note, and Part 4 itself, say this range is narrower than its own standard error implies. They put the decision-matching lower bound at 6.9 months and say Prague's 95 % profile-likelihood region runs from about 14 to 38 months. A reader of the hub gets a much more precise estimate than the study supports.
findings.evidence: assets/praha/housing_extended.json H2.ci90 = [8.72, 12.62]. docs/research/prague-housing-design.md:893-895: "Prague's profile likelihood for μ is flat: the 95 % profile region runs from about 14 to 38 months. It is much wider than the bootstrap interval of the contrast (8.7 to 12.6 months)." texts/prague-housing.html (body): "one-sided lower bound at Holm's threshold ... 6.9 months. The 5th to 95th percentiles ... 8.7 to 12.6 months, are narrower than that standard error implies" and "both bootstrap figures understate how uncertain Prague's own lag is".
findings.fix: Write "(H2 supported, p < 0.001; the bootstrap understates the uncertainty, and the one-sided bound at Holm's threshold is 6.9 months)", or drop the 8.7–12.6 range from the hub.
findings.note: housing_extended.json H2.ci90=[8.72,12.62], se_boot 1.93. prague-housing.html l.151-152 and l.216 call 6.9 months the bound that matches the decision and say the bootstrap figures understate the uncertainty (profile region about 14-38 months). The hub gives 8.7-12.6 with no caveat. Same issue as [10].

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:121 "while by census count its metropolitan region sits in the upper quarter of 208 European regions for 2011–2021"
findings.problem: The hub reports only the favourable ranking. The census count for Czechia includes reconstructions, and on the Czech Statistical Office's count of new completions Part 4 places the same region mid-table. The hub sentence implies Prague builds a lot by European standards, while Part 4 qualifies that claim.
findings.evidence: housing_extended.json H1.raw_rate_ranks: metro_eurostat 5.28, rank 163 of 208 (upper quarter, so the label itself is arithmetically right); metro_csu_rebuilt 3.88, rank 116 of 208, median 3.50. texts/prague-housing.html: "Czechia, Spain and Croatia also count reconstructions" and "Counting only the Czech Statistical Office's completions of new houses gives 3.88, mid-table at 116th of 208".
findings.fix: Write "by census count, which for Czechia includes reconstructions, its metropolitan region sits in the upper quarter of 208 European regions for 2011–2021 (mid-table, 116th, counting new completions only)".
findings.note: H1.raw_rate_ranks: metro_eurostat rank 163/208, metro_csu_rebuilt 116/208 (median 3.50). prague-housing.html l.134-135 notes that Czechia counts reconstructions and that the region is mid-table on ČSÚ new completions. The hub gives only the census rank. Same issue as [16].

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:105 "its gradient across the estates steepened from 0.55 to 0.80 ... Education and citizenship from the 2021 census account for 43 % of that gradient"
findings.problem: "That gradient" follows directly on the 2017→2025 steepening, so a reader can take 43 % as the share of the steepening (or of the 0.80 slope) explained. In fact θ = 0.43 is the share of the 2025 cross-sectional estate gradient on the 282-cluster model, which is a different estimand and sample from the 0.55→0.80 H3 series (819 matched precincts).
findings.evidence: rings_extended.json: H1_ANO.theta 0.426 (2025 cross-section); H3.panel_slope_per10pp_by_year 2017 0.545, 2025 0.801, n_precincts 819. Part 2 deck: "Education and citizenship explain 43 % of the rise in ANO's 2025 vote with the share of panel flats".
findings.fix: Write "Education and citizenship from the 2021 census account for 43 % of ANO's 2025 estate gradient, short of the registered half (H1b not supported)".
findings.note: rings_extended.json H1_ANO.theta=0.426 is the share of the 2025 cross-sectional gradient (rings l.138). The H3 0.545->0.801 series uses 819 matched precincts. In the hub, 'that gradient' directly follows the steepening, so the referent is ambiguous.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:149,151 registration table "3830f59 · 28 Sep 22:39" vs "683b0c8 · 29 Sep 01:19"
findings.problem: The table mixes git timestamp types. Part 1's design time is the author date, while that commit was actually created at 22:57, after the results commit's author time of 22:53. Part 3's design time is the committer date, while its author date is 01:07. Since the table's purpose is to show design-before-results order, using different clocks per row is inconsistent. The Part 1 row also hides that the design and results commits were both written at 22:57 (a rebase or amend).
findings.evidence: git log: 3830f59 author 28 Sep 22:39, committer 28 Sep 22:57; a79f48f author 22:53, committer 22:57; 683b0c8 author 29 Sep 01:07, committer 01:19. The other rows have identical author and committer times.
findings.fix: State which timestamp is shown (e.g. "author time") and use it for every row, giving Part 3 as 01:07. Alternatively add a note that the Part 1 commits were rewritten at 22:57.
findings.note: git log: 3830f59 author 22:39 / committer 22:57; a79f48f author 22:53 / committer 22:57; 683b0c8 author 01:07 / committer 01:19. The table shows author time for Part 1 and committer time for Part 3. Other commits have identical author and committer times.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:168 Part 2 published data: "precincts2025.json · rings_robust.json"
findings.problem: The data table leaves out Part 2's confirmatory results file, rings_extended.json, which holds θ, the H3 gradients and G = 56. Part 2's own text cites that file. The sentence above the table says the numbers behind the figures and tables are published, and every other part lists its *_extended results file.
findings.evidence: assets/praha/rings_extended.json exists. texts/prague-rings.html links assets/praha/rings_extended.json and cites "(rings_extended.json, G = 56)". The hub rows for Parts 1, 3 and 4 list council_extended.json, districts_extended.json and housing_extended.json.
findings.fix: Add rings_extended.json to the Part 2 row.
findings.note: assets/praha/rings_extended.json exists and prague-rings.html cites it (G = 56). The hub's Part 2 row lists only precincts2025.json and rings_robust.json, while the other parts list their *_extended.json.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:113 "was not supported and underpowered (−37 %, 95 % CI −115 to +21 %)"
findings.problem: The registered design fixes the wording for a null H1: it is reported as "inconclusive" (the ±20 % TOST does not reject, since the upper bound is +21 %) and as "not detected". The hub uses neither registered word.
findings.evidence: docs/research/prague-districts-design.md:221-223 "Otherwise it is 'inconclusive'" and :454-457 "A non-rejection is reported as 'not detected', never as 'no premium' ... A null H1 will therefore be reported as 'inconclusive'".
findings.fix: Write "was not supported: inconclusive (underpowered; −37 %, 95 % CI −115 to +21 %)".
findings.note: The design (l.221-223, 454-457) says a null H1 is reported as 'not detected' and the TOST result as 'inconclusive'. The hub, like Part 3's own table (l.145), says 'not supported · underpowered'. The deviation starts in Part 3 itself, yet the hub claims results are reported in the registered wording. Low severity.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:129 "2012's cars would fit about 1.6 % more ..., some 2 800 of 168 400 administrative stalls"
findings.problem: Read side by side, the numbers do not multiply out: 1.6 % of 168 400 is about 2 700, not 2 800. The stall figure comes from a different formula (N·s·(1/(1−θu)−1)) and is right as computed, but a reader checking the arithmetic will see a mismatch.
findings.evidence: assets/parking6/e1.json theta.median 0.01611, extra.median 2756.9. tools/parking6/parking6_estimate.py:376 extra = N_STALLS * s * (1 / (1 - th_u) - 1). 0.0161 × 168 424 = 2 712.
findings.fix: Write "about 2 750" or "some 2 700–2 800", or drop "of 168 400" so the two figures are not read as a direct product.
findings.note: e1.json theta 0.01611, extra 2756.9, and 0.0161*168424 = 2712. Part 5 l.236 also says 'about 2 800'. The rounding mismatch is real but minor.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:84 "bsandova.com/texts/prague-measured, version 2"
findings.problem: The "cite as" line gives version 2, but the page is version 3 (meta line 76 and change log line 183).
findings.evidence: Line 76: "updated 1 October 2026 · version 3". Line 183: "1 October 2026: version 3".
findings.fix: Change to "version 3".
findings.note: The cite-as line says 'version 2'. The meta line 76 and the change log say version 3.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:105 "ANO won 26 % in precincts made up mostly of panel flats and 16 % where there are almost none"
findings.problem: The thresholds behind 26 % and 16 % are more than seven flats in ten in panel buildings and fewer than one in ten. "Mostly" (more than half) and "almost none" misstate those cut-offs.
findings.evidence: Part 2 facts box: "precincts where more than seven in ten flats are in panel buildings 26 % · 16 % where fewer than one in ten are".
findings.fix: Write "26 % where more than seven flats in ten are in panel buildings and 16 % where fewer than one in ten are".
findings.note: Part 2 facts box and l.111/216 use more than seven in ten vs fewer than one in ten. The hub says 'mostly' and 'almost none'.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:162 "All the sources are public: the City Assembly's roll-call records, ... Statistik Austria, Statistics Poland and Eurostat."
findings.problem: The list reads as complete but leaves out sources the parts depend on: the ČÚZK RÚIAN cadastre (Parts 2 and 4), PID GTFS (Parts 2 and 4), the city's paid-parking-zone ArcGIS layer (Part 5), the Chapel Hill expert survey (Part 1, H3) and the ČSÚ candidate registers (Part 3).
findings.evidence: texts/prague-rings.html "Sources: ČSÚ, ČÚZK RÚIAN, PID GTFS"; texts/prague-parking.html "the city's layer of paid parking zones on its ArcGIS server"; texts/prague-council.html "the design used the Chapel Hill expert survey"; texts/prague-districts.html "ČSÚ candidate registers 2014, 2018 and 2022".
findings.fix: Add "the cadastre (RÚIAN), Prague's public-transport timetable (GTFS), the city's paid-parking layer and the Chapel Hill expert survey", or write "Among the sources are ...".
findings.note: The hub's source list leaves out RÚIAN and PID GTFS (rings l.85, housing l.80/266), the city's ZPS ArcGIS layer (parking l.95/273) and CHES (council l.87/169). Candidate registers are arguably covered by 'Czech Statistical Office'. Low severity.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:121 "about 11 months longer ... (H2 supported; bootstrap 90 % interval 8.7 to 12.6)"
findings.problem: The hub gives the narrow bootstrap percentile interval as the uncertainty of the 11-month gap. Part 4 itself rejects that interval: it says the bootstrap understates the uncertainty and that the size of the gap lies somewhere between about 6 (or 3) months and more than 30 months.
findings.evidence: texts/prague-housing.html: "The 5th to 95th percentiles of the bootstrap draws, 8.7 to 12.6 months, are narrower than that standard error implies"; "Fig. 3 shows why both bootstrap figures understate how uncertain Prague's own lag is ... its size lies somewhere between about 6 months (3 if the isolated point at 11 months is counted) and more than 30 months"; the bound that matches the decision is the one-sided 6.9 months.
findings.fix: Replace with: "...about 11 months longer (H2 supported); the sign is firm, but the size is uncertain, from about 6 to over 30 months, and it may partly reflect when completions are registered and project size."
findings.note: Duplicate of [0]. prague-housing.html l.152 and l.216 say the size allows about 6 (3) months to over 30 months, and the bootstrap understates it.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:129 "On today's paid kerb, 2012's cars would fit about 1.6 % more (1.3–1.9 % under the registered inputs), some 2 800 of 168 400 administrative stalls"
findings.problem: The blurb gives the headline kerb estimate without saying it is an upper bound. Part 5's own short version puts that caveat first: every parallel bay is treated as unmarked. The figure is also modelled, not measured.
findings.evidence: texts/prague-parking.html tldr: "The estimate treats every parallel bay as unmarked, so it is an upper bound."; body line ~236: "1.6 % is an upper bound, falling to 1.3 % or 1.0 % if a quarter or half are painted"; "the fleets of 2012 and 2025 are modelled".
findings.fix: "...would fit at most about 1.6 % more on the model (1.3–1.9 % under the registered inputs; 1.0 % if half the parallel bays are painted), some 2 800 of 168 400 administrative stalls..."
findings.note: prague-parking.html tldr l.63 'so it is an upper bound', l.147 painted scenarios 1.3/1.0 %, l.236 'on the model ... modelled'. The hub blurb carries neither the upper-bound nor the modelled caveat.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:113 "was not supported and underpowered (−37 %, 95 % CI −115 to +21 %)"
findings.problem: The blurb gives the pooled −37 % without the caveats Part 3 attaches to it. The negative sign comes from the 2023 change alone, tested on one year where three were planned, so power was below the simulated ~100 %. The sign flips to about +14 % when the ODS districts are left out. The 2018 change alone gives +20 %. A reader of the hub can take the negative number as a finding.
findings.evidence: texts/prague-districts.html tldr: "The negative estimate comes from 2023 and rests on a few districts." "After the 2018 change, a modest premium is not ruled out." Body: "Leaving all of them out turns the estimate to about +14 %"; "the 2023 change is tested on 2023 alone ... so power is weaker than simulated".
findings.fix: Add: "The negative point estimate comes from the 2023 change, measured over one year instead of three, and turns positive without the ODS districts; a premium of the 20 % found elsewhere is not ruled out."
findings.note: Districts tldr l.75-76 ('negative estimate comes from 2023 and rests on a few districts', 2018 premium not ruled out), l.163 (+14 % without ODS), l.201 (2023 tested on 2023 alone). The hub has none of these caveats.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:113 "(−37 %, 95 % CI −115 to +21 %)"
findings.problem: An interval reaching −115 % looks impossible, since a district cannot receive less than nothing. The hub does not explain it, while Part 3 does.
findings.evidence: texts/prague-districts.html: "its interval can reach below −100 % although no district can receive less than nothing; the same estimate on a per-resident scale is −2 800 crowns a year, with a 95 % interval from −8 800 to +1 800".
findings.fix: Give the per-resident version (−2 800 Kč a year per resident, 95 % CI −8 800 to +1 800), or add "in % of the control districts' usual grants, a linear scale that can pass −100 %".
findings.note: Districts l.137 explains the linear scale that can pass −100 % and gives the per-resident figure −2 800 CZK (95 % CI −8 800 to +1 800) at l.67/178. The hub gives −115 % with no explanation.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:105 "Education and citizenship from the 2021 census account for 43 % of that gradient, short of the registered half (H1b not supported)" and "its gradient across the estates steepened from 0.55 to 0.80 ... (H3 supported)"
findings.problem: The hub leaves out the qualifiers Part 2 corrected itself to include. The 43 % is "likely understated" because allocation error is correlated with the housing measure. With age added, composition explains 52 %, about half; Part 2 version 2 withdrew "never half" for this reason. The steepening holds in matched, older precincts with residents not held fixed, so it may reflect who moved in. Part 2's own short version states both caveats.
findings.evidence: texts/prague-rings.html tldr: "with age added, about half"; "The gradient steepened, but that may partly reflect who moved into the estates." Body: "43 % is therefore likely understated"; "With the share of over-65s and under-15s added, composition explains 52 %"; changelog "corrected 'never half'".
findings.fix: "...account for 43 % of that gradient (likely understated; about half with age added), short of the registered half (H1b not supported) ... steepened in the matched precincts, which may partly reflect who moved in (H3 supported)."
findings.note: rings l.149 '43 % is therefore likely understated', changelog l.269 'with age added composition explains 52 %', tldr l.73 'may partly reflect who moved into the estates'. The hub blurb omits both.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:97 "Across 10 565 roll calls since 2010 the same councillors' rate of voting against fell..."
findings.problem: The blurb implies a complete voting record. Part 1 states that the files hold only 55–67 % of the roll calls taken, essentially final votes on adopted resolutions, and that procedural votes and amendments, where opposition is concentrated, are mostly missing. This main measurement-validity limit is absent from the hub.
findings.evidence: texts/prague-council.html: "the files hold between 55 and 67 % of the roll calls taken. The missing ones are procedural votes, agenda changes and amendments"; tldr: "The files hold only final votes on adopted resolutions, so they say nothing about intent."
findings.fix: "Across 10 565 published roll calls since 2010, final votes on adopted resolutions and 55–67 % of all votes taken, the same councillors' rate..."
findings.note: council l.102 and l.241: the files hold final votes on adopted resolutions, 55-67 % of roll calls; tldr l.76. The hub's '10 565 roll calls' carries no such qualifier.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:121 "by census count its metropolitan region sits in the upper quarter of 208 European regions for 2011–2021"
findings.problem: The upper-quarter rank rests on a census count that for Czechia also includes reconstructions. On the Czech Statistical Office's completions of new houses, the same region is mid-table, 116th of 208. The hub gives only the favourable count.
findings.evidence: texts/prague-housing.html: "although Czechia, Spain and Croatia also count reconstructions"; "Counting only the Czech Statistical Office's completions of new houses gives 3.88, mid-table at 116th of 208".
findings.fix: "...sits in the upper quarter of 208 European regions by census count, which for Czechia includes reconstructions, and mid-table on new-build completions."
findings.note: Duplicate of [1]. Verified against housing l.134-135 and housing_extended.json ranks 163 vs 116.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:66-73 details.tldr
findings.problem: The short-version box states no result. All three bullets describe process. It does not say what any part found, what the findings rest on, or what would overturn them, so the hub's most useful content (one supported test per part and the main caveats) is buried in the blurbs.
findings.evidence: tldr bullets: "Each part fixes its hypotheses...", "The order of design and results rests on the author's own git commits...", "Each article ends with what its data do not show."
findings.fix: Add one bullet per part with the headline and its label, for example "Part 4: Prague's permit-to-completion pipeline is longer than the rest of Czechia's (supported), size uncertain", and one bullet on what the series cannot show (no causal effects, self-reported timestamps).
findings.note: The tldr (l.66-73) has three process bullets and no findings or caveats per part. This is factually accurate as an observation, but an editorial judgement.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:147 table header "Design v2 commit"; line 142 "there was no external peer review"
findings.problem: The hub never explains what v1 and v2 of a design are. The design files say v2 was revised after review by "three independent referees", and the hub separately says there was no external peer review. The reader cannot reconcile the two or tell who the referees were.
findings.evidence: docs/research/prague-rings-design.md:3 "Version 2, after review by three independent referees (statistics, electoral geography, census data)"; docs/research/prague-council-design.md:3 "registered (v2, after review) by three referees"; docs/research/prague-housing-referees.md.
findings.fix: Add one sentence: "Each design was revised once (v2) after reports from three referee reviews, linked as <part>-referees.md; these reviews were [internal / by whom], not external peer review."
findings.note: The design headers say v2 was revised after three referee reports (prague-*-referees.md exist). The hub labels the column 'Design v2 commit' and says 'no external peer review', but never explains v2 or the referees.

findings.location: texts/prague-measured.html:97,105,113,121,144
findings.problem: The hub uses technical terms it never explains: "pp" and "per 10 pp of panel flats" (105), "pooled over ... three transitions" (97), "H1b"/"H3" labels and the meaning of "supported/uninformative/indeterminate/inconclusive" (97–129), "underpowered" (113), "bootstrap 90 % interval" (121), "house number" as the marker of completion (121), "in-year grants" as opposed to formula money (113), "administrative stalls" (129), and "Holm's procedure" and "family-wise error rate" (144).
findings.evidence: Searched the hub text: none of these terms is defined there; the definitions appear only inside the individual parts.
findings.fix: Add a short glossary line under "How each part was registered" defining the four labels, Holm and family-wise error, and pp. Gloss "house number (the record of completion)" and "in-year grants (beyond the published formula)" at first use.
findings.note: pp, Holm, family-wise error rate, bootstrap, the label vocabulary, house number and administrative stalls appear in the hub (l.97-144) without definition. Low severity, generic.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html, Praha Sobě row "'Start preparing' 8 000 city flats", Why not: "...and permits in Prague take longer than elsewhere. [12]" (also ratings.json row, ref P4)
findings.problem: The row cites the housing study [12] for the claim that permits take longer in Prague. That study measures the lag from permit to completion. It says explicitly that it does not measure how long the permit itself takes, and that the 11-month gap may partly reflect reporting timing.
findings.evidence: texts/prague-housing.html:153: "The result also says nothing about how long the permit itself took ... The 11 months are therefore a difference in the recorded pipeline, from permit to house number, which may partly be reporting timing".
findings.fix: Reword to: "...and in Prague a permitted flat takes about 11 months longer to be completed than elsewhere in Czechia [12]." In the method paragraph, add "in the recorded pipeline, which may partly be reporting timing" after "about 11 months longer".
findings.note: The note says at line 167 that 'permits in Prague take longer than elsewhere [12]'. prague-housing.html:153 says the 11 months are a gap in the recorded pipeline from permit to house number, may partly be reporting timing, and 'says nothing about how long the permit itself took'. The method paragraph at line 117 also leaves out that caveat.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html, SPD row "Cheaper residents' parking, no further price rises": "Parking-zone prices are set by the city's own regulation. [14]"
findings.problem: Reference [14] is the Prague building regulations (nařízení 12/2024, pražské stavební předpisy). The note's own annotation says they cover parking capacities in new buildings (§25–27). They do not set prices for the paid on-street parking zones. Those prices are set by a separate city regulation on paid parking zones, made under the road traffic and roads legislation. The citation points to the wrong instrument.
findings.evidence: r14 text: "parking capacities in §25–27". The praha.eu page for 12/2024 names it 'o požadavcích na výstavbu' (on building requirements).
findings.fix: Cite the city regulation that sets the paid parking zones and their prices (or §23 of zákon 13/1997 as the legal basis), or drop the [14] link from this reason.
findings.note: The r14 annotation (line 775) is nařízení 12/2024 'o požadavcích na výstavbu', with parking capacities in §25–27. Those are minimums for new buildings, not the prices of paid parking zones. Line 500 cites r14 for zone prices, so the citation points to the wrong instrument.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html intro: "a local coefficient on property tax by area or type of property, but not on empty flats [11]"; Piráti row "Multiple property tax on long-empty and wholly tourist buildings" rated 'state or another body': "The law has no category for empty flats, so a tax aimed at them needs Parliament"; r11 annotation "by area or group of property"
findings.problem: The note says the law lets the city set a local coefficient only by area or by type of property. The current §12 also lets the assembly set a coefficient of 0.5–5 for specific, named properties, by a general measure. So the city could apply a higher coefficient to particular buildings it names, such as long-empty ones, without Parliament. The 'decided by the state' rating and the r11 summary leave this out and overstate the limit.
findings.evidence: zakonyprolidi.cz/cs/1992-338 (current version 1.10.2025), §12 odst. 1 písm. b): "opatřením obecné povahy vydaným zastupitelstvem obce v případě místního koeficientu pro vymezené nemovité věci"; §12ab odst. 5: "se vztahuje na dané seskupení nemovitých věcí nebo danou nemovitou věc"; §12a odst. 2: the properties must be identified per §12e.
findings.fix: Correct r11 and the intro to name the third option (specific, named properties by a general measure). Re-rate the Piráti row, probably to 'partly': the city can raise the coefficient on named properties, but it cannot define a tax by emptiness itself. Alternatively, explain why that option does not apply.
findings.note: I fetched zakonyprolidi 1992-338. §12(1)(b) allows a coefficient 'opatřením obecné povahy vydaným zastupitelstvem obce ... pro vymezené nemovité věci'. §12ab(5) applies it to 'danou nemovitou věc', and §12(4) gives it priority over other coefficients. r11 and the intro at line 116 name only 'area or group', so they leave out this route. That weakens the 'state or another body' rating on the Piráti row (line 273).

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html r13 "Piráti Praha (2026). Program 2026: the first section of metro D in operation in 2032"; cited in the shared summary ("its first section is planned for 2032 [13]") and in the Praha Sobě, STAN and ANO rows ("the first section is planned for 2032, after the term")
findings.problem: The official schedule for metro D is sourced to one competing party's election programme, and that source is then used to judge three other lists. The Piráti page only promises to 'watch the timetable' for opening in 2032. It is not an authoritative statement of the plan.
findings.evidence: program2026.praha.pirati.cz/program/doprava/: "budeme hlídat harmonogram pro zprovoznění prvního provozního úseku metra D v roce 2032" (we will watch the timetable for opening the first section of metro D in 2032).
findings.fix: Cite the builder or the city (DPP / Metro D project pages, or a city council resolution) for the 2032 opening. Keep the Piráti page only as the source for the Piráti row.
findings.note: r13 (line 774) is the Piráti programme page. It is the only source for the 2032 date, and that date is then used in the shared summary (line 124) and in the Praha Sobě, STAN and ANO rows (lines 209, 385, 719). No source from DPP or the city is cited.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html, Praha Sobě row 'yes' "Stop selling city flats and land": "The City Assembly decides on selling city property, so one resolution is enough." / "Nothing in law blocks it"
findings.problem: This contradicts the note itself, which says the districts manage many city flats. The SPD and ANO rows also say "Many flats are managed by the districts, which decide on those." Flats entrusted to a district are sold by that district's own decision. §59(3)(i), cited via [1], reserves to the City Assembly only the transfer of property it manages directly. A 'yes' with 'one resolution is enough' overstates the city's reach.
findings.evidence: Intro: "The city districts ... manage many city flats"; SPD row "Repair empty city flats 'at once'": "Many flats are managed by the districts, which decide on those"; zákon 131/2000 §59 odst. 3 písm. i.
findings.fix: Rate it 'likely', or keep 'yes' and add in Why not: "Flats entrusted to the districts are sold by the districts; stopping that needs a change to the Statute or the districts' agreement."
findings.note: Line 138 says 'one resolution is enough'. The intro at line 116 says the districts manage many city flats, and lines 522 and 691 say the districts decide on those flats. A 'yes' with 'nothing in law blocks it' leaves out the flats entrusted to the districts. That contradicts the note's own text.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html r3: "Zákon č. 561/2004 Sb., školský zákon, §177 odst. 1 (regions establish secondary schools; municipalities kindergartens and primary schools)"
findings.problem: The section number is wrong. §177(1) only says that local self-government in education is exercised by municipalities and regions. Municipalities set up kindergartens and primary schools under §178(1)–(2). Regions set up secondary schools under §181(1)(a).
findings.evidence: zakonyprolidi.cz/cs/2004-561: "§ 177 (1) Územní samosprávu ve školství vykonávají a) obec, b) kraj."; §178(1)–(2) "Obec a) zřizuje a zrušuje základní školu ... mateřskou školu"; §181(1) "kraj zřizuje a zrušuje a) střední školy".
findings.fix: Change to "§178 odst. 1–2 (municipalities: primary schools and kindergartens) and §181 odst. 1 písm. a (regions: secondary schools)".
findings.note: In the fetched 2004-561, §177(1) reads only 'Územní samosprávu ve školství vykonávají a) obec, b) kraj'. The duties of the region are in §181(1), and the founding powers sit in §178 and §181. So the reference to §177(1) at r3 (line 764) does not support the gloss.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html intro: "it orders public transport and sets fares [2]"; SPD row "The city sets public-transport fares through its transport authority. [2] [1]"
findings.problem: The cited §3(1)–(2) of zákon 194/2010 is about regions setting and ensuring transport service. It says nothing about fares, so the fare claim has no cited support.
findings.evidence: zakonyprolidi.cz/cs/2010-194 §3: "Kraje a obce ve své samostatné působnosti stanoví rozsah dopravní obslužnosti a zajišťují dopravní obslužnost..." (no mention of fares).
findings.fix: Add the provision that covers fares (e.g. the tariff provisions of 194/2010 or the price regulation for public transport), or limit the [2] citation to 'orders public transport'.
findings.note: In the fetched 2010-194, §3(1)–(2) covers only setting and ensuring transport service. Fares appear elsewhere in the act ('maximální tarify pro cestující, mají-li být stanoveny objednatelem', in the provisions on the service plan). So the cited §3 does not support 'sets fares' at lines 116 and 479.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html method paragraph: "Promises of 10 000 flats a year cannot be met when about 6 000 are completed now, most of them by private builders"; Piráti row "mostly by private builders"
findings.problem: The 6 000 figure is consistent with [12] (4.5 per 1 000 residents; 6 489 in 2024). The claim 'most of them by private builders' has no source in the note or in the cited housing article.
findings.evidence: grep of texts/prague-housing.html and ratings.json: no figure for the share of completions by builder type.
findings.fix: Cite a ČSÚ breakdown of completions by investor, or drop 'most of them by private builders'.
findings.note: I grepped prague-housing.html. Its only breakdown by builder is for Vienna and Warsaw (fig. 4, lines 159–160). It has no Prague share by investor, and ratings.json has none either. So 'most of them by private builders' (lines 124 and 262) has no source.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html, SPOLU row 'partly' "Raise the tourist fee to the European average": "The city may raise the fee up to the legal ceiling. [6]"; Praha Sobě row: "charge the fee up to the ceiling"
findings.problem: The note never says what Prague charges now. If Prague already charges the statutory maximum of 50 Kč, the city has no room to raise it. In that case the SPOLU row's 'partly' should read 'decided by the state', and this rating would not be consistent with the other tourist-fee rows. As written, the reason cannot be checked.
findings.evidence: Statute checked: zákon 565/1990 §3d "Sazba poplatku z pobytu činí nejvýše 50 Kč" (version 1.1.2025). No figure for Prague's current rate appears anywhere in the note or in ratings.json.
findings.fix: State Prague's current rate with a source (the city's ordinance on the local fees). If it is already 50 Kč, change the SPOLU rating to 'state or another body' and drop 'up to the ceiling' from the Praha Sobě reason.
findings.note: A search found Prague's ordinance OZV 18/2019 Sb. hl. m. Prahy, §3: 'Sazba poplatku činí 50 Kč za osobu a každý započatý den'. Prague already charges the statutory maximum. 'May raise the fee up to the legal ceiling' (line 637) and 'charge the fee up to the ceiling' (line 229) are therefore empty, and the 'partly' on the SPOLU row (line 635) does not hold.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html About box: "the programme texts of six lists, captured 24–29 September 2026"
findings.problem: Every source footer gives the capture date as 29 September 2026. The 24 September date is the date printed on the Praha Sobě PDF, not a capture date, so the range '24–29' mixes the two.
findings.evidence: Section footers: Praha Sobě "PDF dated 24 September 2026, archived 29 September 2026"; all other lists "29 September 2026".
findings.fix: "captured 29 September 2026 (the Praha Sobě PDF is dated 24 September)".
findings.note: Line 105 and ratings.json 'about' both say 'captured 24-29 September'. Every footer gives 29 September as the capture date. 24 September appears only as the date printed on the Praha Sobě PDF (line 238).

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html change log: entries ordered "version 1", "version 3", "version 2"
findings.problem: The change log entries are out of order: version 3 appears between versions 1 and 2.
findings.evidence: Lines rendered: "1 October 2026, version 1 ... version 3 ... version 2".
findings.fix: Order the entries version 3, 2, 1 (or 1, 2, 3).
findings.note: Lines 787–789 list the versions in the order 1, 3, 2.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html:92 (tldr) 'Every programme promises far more housing than Prague can build in four years'
findings.problem: The short version claims more than the ratings show. Not every programme makes an over-scale housing promise. SPD gives no number ('thousands of further flats', and its own 'Overall' says the housing plans 'lack numbers, dates and money'). ANO promises 1 000 city-flat starts a year by the end of the term, and STAN 2 000 starts, both rated 'partly', not 'not in one term'. Only Piráti and SPOLU (10 000 a year, which Piráti calls a long-term goal) and Praha Sobě (8 000 'start preparing', no timeframe) carry large numbers.
findings.evidence: ratings.json rows: SPD 'Cooperative housing ... thousands of further flats' partly; ANO 'Be starting 1 000 city flats a year' partly; STAN 'Start building 2 000 city flats' partly; SPD overall at line 563; Piráti row at line 262 notes the target is long-term.
findings.fix: Use 'Three programmes put numbers on housing (8 000 or 10 000 flats) that Prague cannot complete in four years; the programmes that promise starts (STAN 2 000, ANO 1 000 a year) are closer to what a term allows; SPD gives no number.'
findings.note: Line 92 says 'Every programme promises far more housing than Prague can build'. SPD gives no number: line 533 says 'thousands' and its Overall at line 563 says the housing plans 'lack numbers'. ANO promises 1 000 starts a year (line 681) and STAN 2 000 starts (line 361), both rated partly. So 'every' overstates the ratings.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html:117 'rated ... : yes, likely, partly (with the part that can be done), not in one term, or decided by the state or another body'
findings.problem: The five rating categories are listed but never defined. Nothing says what separates 'yes' from 'likely', or 'partly' from 'not in one term' or 'other'. Without definitions they are applied inconsistently, and the inconsistency changes the headline counts. The same promise gets different ratings across lists: 'Finish building metro D' (Praha Sobě) is 'not in one term', while 'Complete metro D' (STAN) and 'Continue building metro D' (ANO) are 'partly'. A ring metro line is 'not in one term' for Praha Sobě but 'likely' for SPOLU. Raising the tourist fee is 'partly' for SPOLU but sits in 'state or another body' rows for Praha Sobě and Piráti.
findings.fix: Add one sentence per category with its decision rule, e.g. 'not in one term = the promise as worded requires completion that cannot happen by 2030; partly = the city can do a stated first part; other = the decisive step is a law or another body's decision'. Then re-rate the inconsistent rows or explain the wording difference in each row.
findings.note: Lines 117 and 124 and the ratings.json 'about' list the five labels but give no decision rule for any of them. One real inconsistency remains: 'Finish building metro D' is rated 'not in one term' (line 206), while STAN's 'Complete metro D' is rated 'partly' (line 382), with the same reason given (first section in 2032). Some other pairs the auditor cites differ in wording or in what the row bundles.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html:117 'its most concrete and consequential promises were rated ... Rows were chosen per programme'
findings.problem: Row selection is the main limitation of every count, but the text does not explain it. It does not say how many promises each programme contains, what made a promise 'consequential', or whether one row may bundle several promises. Several rows do bundle promises of different feasibility under one rating ('Take over the Na Františku hospital; raise the tourist fee'; 'Prague package ... ; trees, wildlife care'; 'Minimum flat size 16 -> 30 m²; lower parking minimums'). The meta description and og text ('of 80 promises, 29 are within the city's powers') read as a census of the programmes. Selection is also partly author-plus-LLM driven.
findings.evidence: Lines 7, 83, 117; bundled rows at 150, 280, 343. ratings.json 'about' gives no selection rule. No design document exists in docs/research for this note.
findings.fix: State the rule and its coverage near the header, e.g. 'Rows: up to 15 promises per programme, chosen as those with a number, a named project or a legal change; related promises are grouped in one row and rated by the hardest part. The counts depend on this choice.' Repeat 'rows chosen by the author' in the meta description.
findings.note: Line 117 gives 'most concrete and consequential' as the only rule for choosing rows. It gives no coverage and no rule for bundling, although rows 150, 280 and 343 bundle promises. The meta description at line 7 ('of 80 promises, 29 are within...') carries no caveat about row selection.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html:117 'the legal points they rest on were checked against the statutes cited' / :283
findings.problem: The method says the legal points were checked, but one 'likely' rating rests on a legal point the row itself says was not confirmed. That row is 'Minimum flat size 16 -> 30 m²'. The ratings were also drafted by a language model under a 'fixed brief' that is not published, so the claim that one brief was used for all six programmes cannot be checked.
findings.evidence: Line 283: 'Where the 16 m² minimum is set was not confirmed here'. The rating is still 'likely'. ratings.json and tools/notes/programmes_2026.py contain no brief.
findings.fix: Rate that row 'partly', or split it into a parking row (likely) and an unrated flat-size row. Publish the LLM brief next to ratings.json and link it from line 117, or drop 'under one fixed brief'.
findings.note: Line 283 says where the 16 m² minimum is set 'was not confirmed', yet line 280 still rates the row likely. That contradicts line 117, which says the legal points were checked. tools/notes/programmes_2026.py, ratings.json and docs/ contain no brief or prompt.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html:124 'the city has no legal power to restrict short-term rentals'
findings.problem: The overview states an absolute claim that the rows do not support. The STAN row says the city has 'little power' (line 441). Several rows say it 'can enforce existing rules' (lines 229, 549). Reference r15 is a version of the tourism act effective 1 March 2021, which does not cover later legislation (e.g. the EU short-term rental regulation applying from May 2026, or any Czech registry amendment). The tldr (line 94) also says the tourist fee is something 'the state decides', yet SPOLU's fee row is rated 'partly' because the city sets the fee up to the ceiling.
findings.evidence: Line 124 vs lines 229, 441, 549; r15 at line 776; SPOLU row at 635-640.
findings.fix: Use 'state law gives the city no power to restrict short-term rentals as such; it can only enforce existing rules' and cite a current consolidated version. In the tldr, write 'which needs a change in state law above the 50 Kč ceiling'.
findings.note: Line 124 says the city has 'no legal power to restrict short-term rentals', while STAN's row at line 441 says 'little power' and lines 229 and 549 say the city can enforce rules. r15 (line 776) is the 2021 version of the act. One part of the finding is refuted: Prague already charges the 50 Kč cap (see [8]), so the tldr's 'which the state decides' about the fee is correct.

findings.location: texts/prague-programmes-2026.html:89-96 (details.tldr)
findings.problem: The short version gives findings and a scope caveat.
