findings.location: texts/eurovision.html:138 "Two countries sitting together in the European Union does not change what they give each other at all." (also :7 meta description "joining the EU earns a country no points at all", :128 "Leaving the 2004 cohort out, the estimate is −0.32 points (−0.82 to 0.18): nothing.")
findings.problem: The conclusion says EU membership has no effect at all. The registered H3 estimate is a statistically clear fall (−0.91 pp, CI −1.35 to −0.46, about −20 %), not a zero. The 'nothing' rests on one secondary check, and that check does not meet the registered 'not supported' rule either: the margin is ±10 % of the pre-accession mean (±0.45 pp), and the check's interval reaches −0.82 pp. The check also uses a stricter row filter (pairs and years with at least two untreated rows) that was chosen after the first estimates had been printed. So it differs from the main estimate in its sample as well as in its cohort. The article mentions none of this when it says 'almost all of the fall comes from the 2004 enlargement'.
findings.evidence: results.json H3: b=−0.00907, lo=−0.01354, hi=−0.00460, pre_mean=0.0452, label inconclusive. H3_checks.without_2004_cohort: lo=−0.00818, hi=0.00183, n=35071 vs 40412. estimate.py: the main H3 uses the first filter loop; the checks use usable() with value_counts()>1. Design change note of 3 Oct (estimation run), item (2): checks 'added after the first H1–H3 estimates had been printed ... with a stricter filter'.
findings.fix: Line 138: 'Two countries both being in the EU did not raise what they give each other; the registered estimate is a fall of about a fifth, concentrated in the 2004 enlargement, and the study cannot tell whether that fall is real or a by-product of 2004's other changes.' At :128, replace 'nothing' with 'an interval from −0.82 to +0.18 points: still inconclusive under the registered rule, though no longer clearly negative'. Add that this check uses a stricter sample filter, chosen after the main estimate was seen. Change the meta description to 'joining the EU earns a country no extra points'.
findings.note: Same numbers as [0]. Design change note l.197–202 confirms the H3 checks were added after the first estimates had been printed, with a stricter filter: usable() keeps pairs and years with value_counts>1, while the main loop keeps any untreated row. The article mentions neither the post-hoc timing nor the different sample next to 'nothing'.

findings.location: texts/eurovision.html:139 "Free movement, not membership, is what reaches the scoreboard." and "the movement of people the EU made possible ... now sends points back home every May"
findings.problem: This is a causal claim about EU free movement that no analysis here tests. H1 links the migrant stock from any origin to the televote/jury gap. Several of the largest pairs involve migration outside EU free movement: Latvia–Russia, Switzerland–Serbia, Slovenia–Serbia, and Czechia–Ukraine/Russia in fig. 3. Free movement for 2004 entrants also came at accession, which is exactly the treatment that H3 finds raised nothing, or lowered the share. The headline takeaway rests on an inference that was never estimated.
findings.evidence: Table at :93 and fig. 3 text at :113 are dominated by non-EU origins. The design §1 has no hypothesis about free movement. H3 shows a negative or null effect of accession.
findings.fix: Drop the sentence or reword it as speculation: 'Migration, including the migration EU enlargement made easier, does show up on the scoreboard; this study does not separate EU free movement from other migration.'
findings.note: No hypothesis tests free movement. H1 uses migrant stock of any origin. The table includes LV→RU, CH→RS and SI→RS, whose origins are outside EU free movement, and fig. 3 Czechia→UA/RU/MD likewise. 'Free movement, not membership, is what reaches the scoreboard' is an untested causal claim.

findings.location: texts/eurovision.html:40, :42, :106 "At 5.4 migrants per 1 000 inhabitants, the public gives a performer 1.98 times the points the jury gives"; :52 "the public gives that song about twice the points the jury gives"; :138
findings.problem: The text misstates the estimand. R = exp(β·x90) compares the televote-to-jury ratio for a pair at the 90th percentile of diaspora with the same ratio for a pair with no diaspora, all within one voter and one song. It is a ratio of two ratios. It does not mean the public gives 1.98 times the jury's points. The voter×round×audience effects absorb the overall televote and jury levels. Fig. 1 shows that at zero diaspora the public gives about 0.64 times the jury's points, so the two readings are different quantities. Line 101 states the comparison correctly ('against a pair with none'), but the deck, facts box, tldr, body and conclusion all drop it.
findings.evidence: estimate.py: R = exp(b·x90), x90 = 1.856 = log(1+5.4); model points ~ xt | prr + vra + pra. charts.json#gap: under 0.01 per 1 000, televote 1.45 vs jury 2.20.
findings.fix: Say: 'the public's points relative to the jury's are about twice as high for a performer with a large diaspora (5.4 per 1 000) as for one with none.' In the tldr: 'Where many people from the performing country live, the public favours that song over the jury about twice as much as where none do.'
findings.note: estimate.py: R = exp(b·x90), with prr+vra+pra fixed effects, compares the tele/jury ratio at x90 with the ratio at x=0. Descriptively, at <0.01 the ratio is 1.45/2.20 ≈ 0.66, so 'the public gives 1.98 times the points the jury gives' (l.7, l.40, l.42, l.106, tldr l.52) misstates the estimand. Only l.101 states it correctly.

findings.location: texts/eurovision.html:43 "×0.98 ... no difference"; :108 "Neighbours' public votes are 0.98 times their juries' (95 % CI 0.81 to 1.18), and a shared language's 0.91 (0.68 to 1.20): no difference ... the public and the jury favour them equally"; :53 "Diaspora is the one thing only the public brings"
findings.problem: Intervals that include 1 are reported as a finding of equality. By the study's own equivalence margin (0.90 to 1.10), both the neighbour interval (0.81 to 1.18) and the language interval (0.68 to 1.20) would be 'inconclusive'. These are secondary coefficients from a robustness check (§6). They are not registered hypotheses, yet they support the tldr claim that diaspora is 'the one thing only the public brings' and the 'taste rather than loyalty' reading at :138. That claim also generalises from three tested variables to everything. CEPII values are also missing for Montenegro and countries absent from the 2004 file; those cells are treated as 0 (fillna(0)), not left out as the design note says.
findings.evidence: results.json with_contiguity_language: ct b=−0.021 (−0.207 to 0.165) → 0.81 to 1.18; lt b=−0.099 (−0.383 to 0.185) → 0.68 to 1.20. Registered H1 margin is 0.90 to 1.10. estimate.py: h1.contig.fillna(0), h1.comlang.fillna(0). Design note: 'left out of that check only'.
findings.fix: Facts box: 'no clear difference (interval allows ±20 %)'. At :108: 'we find no sign that the public favours neighbours or language-sharers more than the jury, though the intervals allow differences of up to about 20 %'. Tldr: 'Of the things tested, diaspora is the one the public clearly brings and the jury does not.' Either drop the cells with missing CEPII values or disclose that they were counted as non-neighbours.
findings.note: The CIs of 0.81–1.18 and 0.68–1.20 are wider than the 0.90–1.10 margin, and these are secondary §6 check coefficients. estimate.py:63 uses contig.fillna(0)/comlang.fillna(0) after a left merge (prepare.py:235). Design l.165–167 says missing CEPII countries are 'left out of that check only'. The code and the design disagree.

findings.location: texts/eurovision.html:128 "The contests before accession move up and down (fig. 4)"; :131 alt text "estimates before accession move around zero"
findings.problem: The registered pre-trend coefficients (§5) are not reported, and the alt text misdescribes them. Event year −2 is +1.14 pp (CI 0.60 to 1.69): significant, and larger than the headline effect. Year −5 is significantly negative (−0.87 pp), and year −10 is significant too. That is a parallel-trends problem, and it bears directly on whether the −0.91 means anything. Readers are not told this near the result.
findings.fix: Add next to the H3 result: 'Before accession the estimates are not flat: two contests before, pairs gave each other 1.1 points more than expected, more than the size of the post-accession fall, so the comparison group does not track joining pairs well.' Fix the alt text to match.
findings.note: H3_event: evm2 +0.0114 (0.0060 to 0.0169), evm5 −0.0087 (−0.0134 to −0.0040), evm10 lo just above 0. The text says only 'move up and down' / 'noisy'. The alt text says 'around zero', which hides a significant pre-period coefficient larger than the headline effect. Design §5 requires reporting the −10…−2 coefficients with intervals; they appear only in the figure.

findings.location: texts/eurovision.html:122 "The reason is visible in the votes themselves: in 2022 most publics in Europe gave Ukraine their top points, so there was little room left for refugees to add more."
findings.problem: This is a post-hoc explanation of an inconclusive result, stated as fact. It was not tested. The post period runs 2022–2025, not only 2022, and the outcome is televote minus jury, which also depends on what juries gave. A ceiling in 2022 alone cannot account for the whole post period. The interval (−1.06 to +1.22) is simply wide: about 42 voters and one unit of a log measure.
findings.evidence: prepare.py: post = year >= 2022, outcome diff = tele − jury, finals with Ukraine. results.json H2: n=300, voters=42, se=0.58. Design §4 calls H2 a 'second, smaller test'.
findings.fix: 'One possible reason, not tested here: in 2022 most publics gave Ukraine their top points, leaving little room for differences between countries. The test also has only 42 voting countries, so its interval is wide.'
findings.note: l.122 states the ceiling explanation as fact ('The reason is visible...'), but it was not tested. H2: n=300, voters=42, se 0.58, CI −1.06 to 1.22. The post period runs from 2022 on, and the outcome is tele minus jury, so a 2022 ceiling alone does not explain the result.

findings.location: texts/eurovision.html:129 "Leaving cost no points either."
findings.problem: An exploratory estimate whose interval includes zero is stated as a finding. The interval (−0.59 to +1.90 pp, against a mean share of about 4.5 %) allows anything from a loss of about 13 % to a gain of about 40 %, from 679 rows.
findings.evidence: results.json brexit: b=0.0066, lo=−0.0059, hi=0.0190, n=679.
findings.fix: 'The estimate is +0.66 points with a wide interval (−0.59 to 1.90); this exploratory comparison cannot tell whether leaving cost or gained anything.'
findings.note: brexit b=0.0066, CI −0.0059 to 0.0190, n=679. 'Leaving cost no points either' asserts a null from a wide exploratory interval that allows about −13% to +40% of a 4.5% mean.

findings.location: texts/eurovision.html:105 heading "What diaspora does"; :108 "Diaspora is different. It reaches only the phones."; :138 "the largest thing a public adds to a jury's verdict is its migrants"
findings.problem: The text uses causal and attributive language, saying migrants themselves cast the extra votes, but the design shows an association. The audience contrast removes what both audiences share. It does not remove public-only affinities that rise with migration: media exposure, familiarity among non-migrants, and Russian-speaking minorities not born in Russia (Latvia–Russia, 62.9 per 1 000). Also, 'largest thing' is unsupported: only diaspora, contiguity and language were tested. The limitation section (:144) says the study cannot tell why migrants vote, but it assumes they are the ones voting.
findings.evidence: Design §9: 'Why diaspora votes' not shown. Model terms tested: xt, ct, lt only (estimate.py).
findings.fix: Rename the heading 'Where diaspora is large'. Replace 'It reaches only the phones' with 'It shows up only in the public vote'. At :138: 'Of what we tested, the clearest thing a public adds to a jury's verdict follows its migrants.' Next to the H1 result, add that migrant stock may also stand for the wider public's familiarity with the origin country.
findings.note: Only xt, ct and lt were tested (estimate.py), so 'the largest thing a public adds' is unsupported. The design is associational. 'It reaches only the phones' and 'What diaspora does' imply that migrants cast the votes, which the limitations paragraph itself says cannot be shown.

findings.location: texts/eurovision.html:48-55 details.tldr
findings.problem: The short version states results but not what they rest on: a registered design, 9 contests (2016–2025), 45 countries, the same voter's jury and public scoring the same song, and the third of pairs dropped for lack of a UN figure. It also does not say what would overturn the findings, for example the diaspora measure standing for public familiarity rather than migrants voting, or pre-trends in the EU test. The EU bullet does not give the registered label ('inconclusive').
findings.evidence: Lines 51–54 contain no sample, registration or overturn conditions. The facts box at :45 has the counts, but the tldr does not.
findings.fix: Add one bullet: 'Based on a registered analysis of 9 contests (2016–2025) and 45 countries, comparing each country's jury and public on the same song; a third of country pairs have no UN migrant figure. It would be overturned if migrant numbers mainly track how familiar the wider public is with a country, rather than migrants voting.' Label the EU result 'inconclusive under the registered rule'.
findings.note: The EU bullet omits the registered label 'inconclusive' and says 'does not survive leaving it out', which repeats [1]'s overstatement. Requiring sample and overturn conditions in the tldr is an editorial preference. No other article's tldr (texts/*.html) follows that convention.

findings.location: texts/eurovision.html:122 "+0.08 points per unit of the refugee measure (−1.06 to 1.22)"
findings.problem: The 'refugee measure' is never defined in the article. In the code it is log(1 + Ukrainian refugees per 1 000 inhabitants, end 2022), so 'per unit' means nothing to a reader. The registered ±0.5 margin that makes this 'inconclusive' is not stated either.
findings.evidence: prepare.py: h2.ref_x = np.log1p(ref_per1000) at 2022. Design §4 label: not supported if within ±0.5.
findings.fix: '+0.08 televote-minus-jury points to Ukraine for each step of log(1 + refugees per 1 000 inhabitants), roughly a 2.7-fold rise in refugees (95 % CI −1.06 to 1.22); the registered rule needed the interval inside ±0.5 to call it a null, so it is inconclusive.'
findings.note: The article never defines 'unit of the refugee measure' (log1p of refugees per 1 000 in prepare.py). The ±0.5 'not supported' margin (design l.77) is not stated, so a reader cannot see why the result is inconclusive.

findings.location: texts/eurovision.html:42-45, 100, 101, 111, 127-132
findings.problem: Several technical terms are used without explanation at first use. Line 42: '95 % CI' (facts box, before any definition). Line 44: 'pp' and 'years 0 to +5'. Line 45: 'administrative count'. Line 100: 'Poisson regression, estimated by pseudo-maximum likelihood', 'fixed levels' (a non-standard name for fixed effects), and 'Standard errors are clustered by pair of countries'. Line 101: 'the estimate's interval lies wholly above zero' refers to β on the log scale, while the reader has only been given the ratio, whose threshold would be 1. Line 111: 'log scale'. Line 127: 'two-stage difference in differences', 'staggered timing'. Line 128: 'cohort' ('the 2004 cohort'). Line 131: 'event study'. Line 132: 'reference year −1'.
findings.evidence: No glossary or inline definition appears before these uses.
findings.fix: Add short glosses at first use. 'CI: the range the true value plausibly lies in.' 'pp: percentage points of the share of points.' 'Fixed effects: a separate baseline for each voter-round-audience, so only differences within it count.' 'Clustered: allowing votes within the same pair to be correlated.' Restate the rule on the ratio scale ('ratio's interval wholly above 1'). 'Cohort: the countries that joined in the same year.' 'Reference year −1: the last contest before joining, set to zero.'
findings.note: One concrete inconsistency: l.101 defines the ratio and then says 'supported if the estimate's interval lies wholly above zero', which is the log-scale β threshold, while the reader works with the ratio (threshold 1). The other items (CI, pp, cohort, event study, 'fixed levels') are undefined jargon, but adding glosses is a lower-priority editorial fix.

findings.location: texts/eurovision.html:106 "The estimate rests on 11 316 rows, the pair-rounds in which either audience gave a point."
findings.problem: Each row is a pair-round-audience, so 11 316 rows is about 5 658 pair-rounds, not 11 316 pair-rounds.
findings.evidence: prepare.py builds rows per (year, r, i, j, aud). results.json H1 n=11316. Design note: '17 372 → about 11 300 cells'.
findings.fix: 'The estimate rests on 11 316 rows (about 5 660 pair-rounds, each counted once for the public and once for the jury) in which either audience gave a point.'
findings.note: Duplicate of [3]. 11316 long rows (one per audience) correspond to about 5658 pair-rounds. The fig. 1 cells sum to 8686 = 17372/2.

findings.location: texts/eurovision.html:84 "The jury hardly moves with diaspora at all; the public does."
findings.problem: The descriptive figures do not support 'hardly at all'. Average jury points rise from 2.2 to 3.1 across the bins (+42 %), while televote points rise from 1.45 to 5.98.
findings.evidence: charts.json#gap table: jury 2.20, 2.47, 2.82, 2.96, 3.13; televote 1.45 to 5.98.
findings.fix: 'The jury rises a little with diaspora, from 2.2 to 3.1 points; the public rises fourfold.'
findings.note: charts.json gap: jury 2.20, 2.47, 2.82, 2.96, 3.13, a rise of about 42%, and televote 1.45 → 5.98. 'The jury hardly moves with diaspora at all' overstates the contrast.

findings.location: texts/eurovision.html:107 "Compared with each of the five jurors separately ... it is 2.24."
findings.problem: The coverage restrictions of this check are not given where its result appears. It covers only 2016–2022 (the Mirovision juror file) and uses rank-converted points. They appear only in the Changes section.
findings.evidence: estimate.py: tele restricted to 2016–2022 for the juror check. Design change note.
findings.fix: 'Compared with each of the five jurors separately (2016–2022, the years with juror rankings), it is 2.24.'
findings.note: estimate.py:78 restricts tele to 2016–2022 and maps the jurors' ranks to points. l.107 gives 2.24 with no window or method. The restriction appears only in the Changes section.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:121 and :175, "so the registered label is underpowered" / "which is why the "unsure" variant is in the robustness table"
findings.problem: The registered deviation says that if linking recall still differs by group after rule 4, Q1 O1 must report the §6 linking bounds (unmatched projects in both groups counted as released) as its primary range. Rule 4 added only 3 links and recall still differs (91 % against 82–87 %), so that rule applies. The article reports the point estimate +39 pp as primary, and the §6 bound is never computed. The 'unsure counted as released' variant takes its place, but it is not the registered bound.
findings.evidence: docs/research/film-fund-design.md:157-158: "If recall still differs by group after rule 4, Q1 O1 reports the bounds from the §6 sensitivity as its primary range." Line 169: "so Q1 O1 is reported with the §6 bounds." §6 line 116: "unmatched projects in both groups counted as released, to bound the effect of linking errors." tools/film/analyse.py sensitivity dict holds only O1_unsure_as_released (linked_sens), with no bound variant. results.json has no bound entry.
findings.fix: Compute the registered §6 bound and report it as the primary range for O1. If that is not done, list the omission under 'What changed after registration' and drop the claim that the unsure variant is the registered response.
findings.note: design.md:157-158 and 169 commit O1 to the §6 bounds as primary range; analyse.py sensitivity dict has no bound variant (only linked_sens); results.json has no bound; article headlines +39 pp and presents the unsure variant as the response. Duplicate of [14].

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:169, "Only the donut variant excludes zero, and one of seven variants doing so is what chance alone would produce often."
findings.problem: This is false as written. The half-bandwidth variant's interval (−323 to −46) also excludes zero, and it is shown in the table two lines above. So two of seven variants exclude zero, and they point in opposite directions.
findings.evidence: results.json sensitivity.O1_half_bw lo −3.234, hi −0.4569 (pv 0.0092). Table row at line 160: "+3 pp 95 % CI −323 to −46".
findings.fix: Write: "Apart from the half-bandwidth variant, which is unstable and not read, only the donut variant excludes zero…" Or say that two variants exclude zero, in opposite directions.
findings.note: results.json O1_half_bw lo -3.234, hi -0.4569 excludes zero; table row line 160 shows it. The note on line 169 sets the half-bw aside as unstable a sentence earlier, but 'Only the donut variant excludes zero' is still literally false. Duplicate of [17].

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:48, :110, :145, :147-148, "254 released projects" / "Among the 254 projects from these calls that reached cinemas … the median was 14 100"
findings.problem: Q2 is computed on every application from 2016–2021, not on first applications. So the 254 counts applications, and a film that applied in several calls appears several times, both in ρ and in the median. It also keeps only admissions above 0. The primary sample of 588 has only 220 linked projects, 200 of them with admissions above 0, and their median admissions are 9 720, not 14 100. 'Projects' and 'from these calls' therefore misdescribe the unit and inflate n.
findings.evidence: tools/film/analyse.py main(): res["Q2"] = q2(d[d.year <= 2021]), with no d["first"] filter. q2() keeps s.adm > 0. Recomputed from assets/film/applications.csv (primary sample): linked 220, admissions >0 200, median 9 720. results.json Q2.n 254, median_admissions 14133.
findings.fix: Either restrict Q2 to first applications (or deduplicate by project) and rerun, or relabel it as '254 applications (some projects counted more than once)' and state that the median 14 100 is over applications.
findings.note: analyse.py:145 q2(d[d.year<=2021]) has no first filter. Recomputed from applications.csv (first apps, linked, adm>0, calls with >=2): 195 rows in 31 calls, median about 12 200 (not the 9 720 the finding gives; unit problem stands). Reported 254/32 includes repeat applications.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:99 and :182, "Within five points of the cut-off there are about 250 applications … about 25 percentage points would be detected" / "with 182 applications near the line, an effect smaller than about 25 points cannot be told apart from none"
findings.problem: The 25 pp detectable effect comes from the design-stage count of 249 applications within ±5 points. The analysed sample (first applications only) has 175 within ±5 and 182 within the 5.1 bandwidth. Line 182 ties '25 points' to 182 applications, which is internally inconsistent, and with ~180 the detectable effect is larger than 25 pp. The registered design also says 'about 0.2' in prose (§5 line 102) but 0.25 in the table.
findings.evidence: docs/research/film-fund-design.md:99 "±5 points | 249 | 128 / 121 | about 0.25". assets/film/applications.csv: rows with |points_from_cutoff| ≤ 5 = 175. results.json Q1.O1_release n_left 88 + n_right 94 = 182.
findings.fix: Say the 25 pp figure was computed at design stage for ~250 applications (all applications, including repeats), and that the analysed first-application sample has ~180 near the line, so the detectable effect is larger. Remove the pairing of '182 applications' with '25 points'.
findings.note: design.md:99 gives 249 within ±5 (all applications); applications.csv has 175 with |dist|<=5; results n_left+n_right = 182. Line 182 pairs 182 with the 25 pp figure; design prose says 'about 0.2' vs table 0.25.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:192, "Every number on this page is read from assets/film/results.json"
findings.problem: Many numbers on the page are not in results.json, and some cannot be traced anywhere in the repo: the median total budgets (6.0 vs 12.0 million Kč), 'asked … about a third of their budget', the near-miss release shares (54 % / 54 % / 25 %), the kind-of-project table, the median award of 1.5 million, applications per call, the cut-off range, and the recall figures. The budget figures and 'a third' cannot be reproduced from any committed file, because applications.csv has no budget or requested column.
findings.evidence: assets/film/results.json keys: sample, density_p, balance, Q1, sensitivity, rejected_near_cut_later_funded, Q2. None of these holds budgets, kind shares or near-miss release shares. grep of tools/film/figures.py finds no budget/median code. Budget columns are absent from assets/film/applications.csv. The other descriptive numbers do recompute from applications.csv (median award 1 500 000; 14.5 apps per call, 2–30; funded share 43.3 %; cut-off 61.4–84.1, median 75.7; kind table matches; 30 of 88 near misses released, consistent with 28×54 % + 60×25 %).
findings.fix: Write the descriptive numbers, including budget medians and the requested share, into results.json, or publish the budget and requested columns. Otherwise change the sentence to say which numbers come from results.json and which from applications.csv.
findings.note: results.json (identical to docs/research copy) has only sample, density_p, balance, Q1, sensitivity, rejected_near_cut_later_funded, Q2. No budget columns in applications.csv; no budget-median code in tools/film. Line 192 'Every number' is false.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:152-169, Robustness table

The '2016–2022' variant was registered as 'O1 within three years' but is run on release by 30 Sept 2026 with no three-year window.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:187, "about one in ten unmatched applications in the audit, slightly more often among unfunded ones"
findings.problem: In the audit, released films were found under another title for 3/30 funded and 2–3/30 unfunded unmatched applications, so the miss rate per unmatched application is not higher among unfunded ones. It is the recall (share of released films found) that is lower for unfunded projects, because they have fewer linked releases.
findings.evidence: docs/research/film-fund-recall-audit.csv: 5 yes, 1 unsure, 53 no, 1 exists-not-released. Design table at lines 163-166: funded 3, unfunded 2 + 1 unsure.
findings.fix: Write: "about one in ten unmatched applications in the audit; because fewer unfunded projects were linked, the share of released films missed is somewhat higher among unfunded ones (recall about 91 % against 82–87 %)".
findings.note: Audit: funded 3/30 found, unfunded 2/30 + 1 unsure, so the miss rate per unmatched application is equal or near-equal. Recall per released film is lower for unfunded (82-87 vs 91 %), so 'misses ... more often among unfunded' holds in recall terms. The appositive makes it ambiguous. A wording nit, not a factual error.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:98, "a test of whether applications bunch on one side of the cut-off[4]"
findings.problem: The test that was run is the local-polynomial density test from rddensity (Cattaneo, Jansson and Ma), not McCrary's binned density test. Citing only McCrary [4] attributes the test that was run to the wrong source.
findings.evidence: tools/film/analyse.py: `dens = rddensity(X=prim.dist..., c=0)`, p from dens.test['p_jk']. Reference r4 is McCrary (2008). Crossref confirms its metadata.
findings.fix: Add Cattaneo, M. D., Jansson, M., Ma, X. (2020), 'Simple local polynomial density estimators', JASA 115(531), 1449–1455, doi:10.1080/01621459.2019.1635480, as the test used, and keep McCrary as the origin of the idea.
findings.note: analyse.py:127 uses rddensity (Cattaneo-Jansson-Ma local polynomial density test), p_jk; the article cites only McCrary [4] for the test. r3 mentions the rddensity software but not the CJM paper.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:205-215, reference numbering

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:127, "of the 60 that never received support from these calls, 25 %"
findings.problem: 'From these calls' suggests the 2016–2021 production calls, but the later-funding check searches all production calls up to 2026.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:145, "Until 2025 the Council's criteria rated artistic quality, the project's contribution to Czech cinema, the team and the production plan, and none of them asked about audiences; the criterion "potential for an audience" was introduced in the 2025 scheme"
findings.problem: This is a factual claim about the fund's scoring criteria with no source. Before 2025 the fund's production evaluation also scored economic and production elements such as distribution strategy, which arguably concern audiences, so 'none of them asked about audiences' may be overstated.
findings.evidence: No citation in the sentence. The design (§4, line 83) mentions only that 'Potenciál pro publikum' exists from 2025.
findings.fix: Cite the fund's evaluation criteria (call documentation for 2016–2021 and the 2025 scheme), and soften this to 'no criterion was explicitly about audience potential' if distribution strategy was scored.
findings.note: The sentence on line 145 about pre-2025 criteria has no citation; design §4 only mentions 'Potenciál pro publikum' from 2025. I did not verify whether earlier criteria scored distribution strategy, so the 'none asked about audiences' overstatement itself is unverified.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:121, 182 "an effect smaller than about 25 points cannot be told apart from none" / "with 182 applications near the line, an effect smaller than about 25 points cannot be told apart from none"
findings.problem: The 25 pp figure is the design-stage power for about 249 applications within ±5 points (all applications, no clustering, no bias correction). The analysis actually uses 182 first applications, and its robust interval runs from -14 to +100, a half-width of about 57 pp. Effects up to about 50 pp can't be told from zero, so the text overstates the precision by about 2x and pairs the 25 pp figure with the wrong n.
findings.evidence: design.md:96-100 gives 249 applications within ±5, MDE about 0.25 (and line 102 says 'about 0.2'). results.json Q1.O1_release: n_left 88 + n_right 94 = 182, lo -0.1395, hi 0.9954. The primary sample is filtered to d['first'] (analyse.py:125), which the power table did not use.
findings.fix: Say: "The design expected to detect about 25 pp with ~250 applications; the analysis uses 182 first applications clustered in 37 calls, and the realised interval (-14 to +100) means effects as large as about 50 pp cannot be told apart from none." Drop the '182 ... 25 points' pairing in 'What this means'.
findings.note: Same as [3]. The realised robust CI of -14 to +100 has a half-width of about 57 pp, so the '182 ... 25 points' pairing on line 182 overstates precision. The exact '~50 pp' MDE is approximate but the direction is right.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:110, 145, 148 "Among the 254 projects from these calls that reached cinemas"
findings.problem: The Q2 sample counts applications, not projects. analyse.py runs q2() on d[d.year<=2021] without the first-application filter, so a project that applied in several calls appears several times with the same admissions figure. That inflates n, and the median admissions and the bootstrap interval treat these duplicates as independent observations. The design (§2) keeps first applications for the primary analysis.
findings.evidence: analyse.py:146 res['Q2']=q2(d[d.year<=2021]) has no d['first']. If I recompute from the published assets/film/applications.csv (first applications only), linked & cz_admissions>0 in calls with ≥2 gives 195 rows in 31 calls, against the reported 254 in 32 calls. So about 59 rows are repeat applications.
findings.fix: Restrict Q2 to first applications (or deduplicate by project) and re-run. If not, say: "254 applications from 32 calls, which include repeat applications of the same film". In either case, change 'projects' to the correct unit in the facts, table, text and fig. 3 caption.
findings.note: Reproduced: first applications only give 195 rows in 31 calls, against the reported 254 in 32. The article calls them 'projects' on lines 48, 110, 145 and 148.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:175 "which is why the 'unsure' variant is in the robustness table"
findings.problem: Registered change (1)/(2) committed that, because recall differs by group, Q1 O1 would be reported with the §6 bounds (unmatched projects in both groups counted as released) as its primary range. The bounds were never computed. The article substitutes an 'unsure links counted as released' variant, which only moves 11 hand-review rows, and keeps the +39 pp point estimate as the headline. Neither the substitution nor the dropped commitment is disclosed.
findings.evidence: design.md:116 lists 'unmatched projects in both groups counted as released, to bound the effect of linking errors'. design.md:157-158 says 'If recall still differs by group after rule 4, Q1 O1 reports the bounds from the §6 sensitivity as its primary range'. design.md:169 says 'so Q1 O1 is reported with the §6 bounds'. analyse.py:132-139 has no bounds variant, only O1_unsure_as_released (linked_sens, freeze_links.py UNSURE set of 11 rows).
findings.fix: Compute the registered bounds and report them as the O1 primary range in the facts, the tests table and the summary. If that isn't done, add an entry under 'What changed after registration' saying the bounds were replaced by the 'unsure' variant and why.
findings.note: Same as [0]. linked_sens moves only the unsure hand-review rows. The §6 bound (unmatched in both groups counted as released) is never computed, and the substitution is not disclosed under changes.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:152-169 (Robustness) and 172-178 (What changed after registration)
findings.problem: Several registered analyses are missing from the article, and the changes section does not mention them: O3 (European admissions, secondary outcome); call fixed effects as a robustness check; the feature-length-only sensitivity; Q2 for each criterion with a fixed meaning; short-film calls reported separately.
findings.evidence: design.md:51 (O3), 79 (call FE), 83 (per-criterion Q2), 113 ('feature-length only'), 39 (short films separately). analyse.py computes none of them. eu_admissions is collected in link.py but never used.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:163 "Calls of 2016–2022"
findings.problem: The design registered this sensitivity as '2016–2022 for O1 within three years', which gives every call the same follow-up window. The code instead uses release by 30 September 2026 for all calls, so 2022 projects get less time than the others. This undisclosed change to the outcome definition biases the variant toward zero.
findings.evidence: design.md:45 and 114 say O1 within three years. analyse.py:136 is rd(d[(d.year<=2022)&d['first']], 'linked'), and 'linked' is release at any date up to the cut-off date.
findings.fix: Implement release within three years of the call for this variant. Otherwise relabel the row "Calls of 2016–2022, release by 30 Sep 2026 (deviates from the registered three-year window)" and list it under changes.
findings.note: analyse.py:138 rd(d[(d.year<=2022)&d['first']],'linked'): there is no three-year window, while design.md:45/114 registered 'O1 within three years'. The row label on line 163 says only 'Calls of 2016-2022'.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:169 "Only the donut variant excludes zero"
findings.problem: This is false. The half-bandwidth O1 interval (-323 to -46 pp) also excludes zero, in the negative direction, and so does the computed but unpublished O2 half-bandwidth interval (-32.05 to -3.45). Across bandwidths the point estimate ranges from +3 to +57 pp. The +39 headline therefore depends on the bandwidth, and the summary doesn't say so.
findings.evidence: results.json sensitivity.O1_half_bw lo -3.234 hi -0.4569 pv 0.0092; O2_half_bw lo -32.05 hi -3.45; O1_donut +0.57 (0.06 to 1.22); O1_double_bw +0.25.
findings.fix: Write: "Two variants exclude zero, in opposite directions: the donut (+57 pp) and the halved bandwidth (interval entirely negative, unstable with 57 applications). Point estimates range from +3 to +57 pp across bandwidths." Add one clause to 'What this means' saying the size is bandwidth-dependent.
findings.note: O1_half_bw CI (-3.234, -0.457) excludes zero, and so does O2_half_bw (-32.05, -3.45, not published). Point estimates across bandwidths: +3, +25, +39, +57 (donut).

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:112, 116 "the producer's earlier funded applications −2.2 (−7.4 to +2.8)"
findings.problem: The covariate is miscomputed. The data are sorted by project title before the per-producer cumulative count, so 'earlier' means alphabetically earlier project titles of the same company, not applications earlier in time. Later calls (up to 2026) can also count. One of the four balance checks therefore doesn't measure what the text describes.
findings.evidence: analyse.py:72 is d=d.sort_values(['project','year','call']), and project = norm(title)+'|'+company. analyse.py:74 is d.groupby(company).funded.transform(lambda s: s.shift().fillna(0).cumsum()), which uses the row order inside each group.
findings.fix: Sort by ['year','call'] (or by call date) before the groupby-shift-cumsum, re-run the balance check, and update the number.
findings.note: analyse.py:69 sorts by ['project','year','call'], and line 71 does a groupby(company) shift().cumsum(), which follows row order (alphabetical by project) and includes later calls up to 2026. 'Earlier' is therefore not temporal.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:85 "production calls of 2016–2021 for feature fiction, documentary, animation and minority co-production" / 139 note
findings.problem: The sample includes animation series and combined development-and-production calls, whose output mostly goes to television. For these projects O1 (Czech cinema release) is close to 0 whatever the funding decision. This measurement-validity problem is disclosed only in a note under a descriptive table. It is not mentioned in the Data section, near the main estimate or in the summary, and the registered feature-length-only sensitivity that would address it was not run.
findings.evidence: analyse.py:55 keeps every call_title containing 'výrob' except shorts. applications.csv shows animation n=89, with 19 % of funded and 10 % of unfunded projects released. design.md:113 lists feature-length-only.
findings.fix: In the Data section, say that series and development+production animation calls are included and that their release outcome is mostly structurally zero. Run and report the feature-length-only variant next to the main estimate.
findings.note: The disclosure is only in the note on line 139 and the text on line 140; the Data section (line 85) does not mention series or development+production calls. The feature-length-only sensitivity (design.md:113) is not run. Animation release is 19 % / 10 %.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:97 "every looser match was checked by hand"
findings.problem: Registered rule 2 required, in addition to similarity ≥ 0.90, the same producer company where LUMIERE gives one. The code applies no producer check, and this deviation isn't disclosed. The article also leaves out that rule 1 matches were hand-checked only in a 10 % sample.
findings.evidence: design.md:65-66 sets the producer condition. link.py:91-96 checks only token_set_ratio ≥ 90 and a unique best candidate.
findings.fix: Add to 'What changed after registration': "Rule 2 was run without the producer condition, because LUMIERE's producer field was not collected; every rule-2 link was hand-reviewed instead."
findings.note: link.py:84-92 rule 2 checks only token_set_ratio >= 90 and a unique best candidate, with no producer condition, while design.md:65-66 requires one. The deviation is not disclosed. The article's 'An exact match ... counted directly' also leaves out the 10 % rule-1 hand sample.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:45, 57, 182 "funded projects reached Czech cinemas more often" / "Just above the line, more projects reached cinemas" / "the sign of the estimate points that way"
findings.problem: The deck and the TL;DR state that funded projects released more often, but the interval includes zero and the registered label is 'underpowered'. 'What this means' and line 126 ('read here only by its sign') lean on the sign of an estimate whose interval includes zero, while the halved-bandwidth interval is entirely negative. Line 182 also turns 'released in Czech cinemas' into 'whether a film is made'.
findings.evidence: results.json O1 lo -0.14, hi 0.995, label underpowered. O2 lo -2.30. O1_half_bw interval below zero.
findings.fix: Deck: "the estimated jump in release at the cut-off is positive but its interval includes zero (underpowered)". TL;DR: "The estimate points to more releases just above the line, but zero is within its range." Line 182: replace 'decides if a film is made' with 'changes whether a film reaches Czech cinemas', and drop 'the sign points that way'.
findings.note: The deck and TL;DR are already hedged ('labelled underpowered', 'too few to be sure'), so those parts are largely addressed. Line 182 does slide from 'reaches Czech cinemas' to 'decides if a film is made' and leans on the sign while the half-bw interval is negative. That part is confirmed.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:121 "were linked to a release in Czech cinemas"
findings.problem: Five linked projects with 0 Czech admissions in LUMIERE count as 'released in Czech cinemas' in O1 (one of them inside the bandwidth, funded, +4.08). The design defines LUMIERE release as Czech admissions above 0.
findings.evidence: link.py candidates() sets released_cz but never filters on it. applications.csv rows with linked=True & cz_admissions==0: Obléhání města, Auta, kterými jsme přijeli do kapitalismu (+4.08, funded), Amoosed!, Světla, La reine. design.md:49.
findings.fix: Treat LUMIERE-only links with 0 Czech admissions as unreleased, as the design specifies, or disclose the exception.
findings.note: applications.csv has 5 linked rows with cz_admissions == 0, including 'Auta, kterými jsme přijeli do kapitalismu' (+4.08, funded) and Amoosed! (+8.64). Both are rule-2 LUMIERE links in film-fund-links.csv. design.md:49 requires LUMIERE Czech admissions above 0.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:145 "the interval excludes a strong positive relation but cannot tell a weak one from none"
findings.problem: The upper bound is +0.04, so the interval excludes any positive rank correlation above 0.04, weak ones included. The sentence understates what the data rule out, which bears on the practical reading.
findings.evidence: results.json Q2 hi 0.039.
findings.fix: Write: "the interval rules out any positive relation larger than about 0.04, but cannot tell a weak negative one from none".
findings.note: Q2 hi = 0.039, so the interval excludes any positive rho above about 0.04. 'Cannot tell a weak one from none' misstates this; only weak negative or near-zero relations remain.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:53-61 (details.tldr)
findings.problem: The short version gives no numbers and doesn't say what the result rests on: 182 first applications near the line in 37 calls, cinema release found by title linking with about 82-91 % recall, and Czech cinemas only (TV and streaming are invisible). It also doesn't say what would overturn it, for example the result changing with the bandwidth or the half-bandwidth estimate turning negative. The later-funding bullet is not marked as exploratory.
findings.evidence: tldr lines 56-59 contain no n, no interval, no limitation, no falsifier.
findings.fix: Add a bullet such as: "Rests on 182 applications near the line in 37 calls, release found by matching titles (about 9 in 10 found) and Czech cinemas only; a larger sample or bandwidth choices can move the estimate from +3 to +57 pp."
findings.note: TL;DR lines 56-59 contain no n, interval, data limitation or falsifier, and the later-funding bullet is not marked as exploratory. An editorial point, correctly described.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:96 "running variable … estimand … local linear fit on each side, a triangular kernel, the bandwidth that minimizes mean squared error, and robust bias-corrected 95 % confidence intervals clustered by call"
findings.problem: The central method terms are used without explanation at first use: running variable, estimand, regression discontinuity (first named here, line 96), local linear fit, triangular kernel, bandwidth/MSE-optimal, robust bias-corrected, clustered by call.
findings.evidence: None of these is defined anywhere in the text; only 'effective sample' is.
findings.fix: Add one plain gloss for each, e.g. "bandwidth: how many points either side of the line are used", "triangular kernel: projects closer to the line count more", "clustered by call: projects in the same call are not treated as independent".
findings.note: Line 96 uses running variable, estimand, local linear, triangular kernel, MSE-optimal bandwidth, robust bias-corrected and clustered by call with no gloss; only 'effective sample' is defined.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:45 "the Council's points"; 47 "pp"; 48 "ρ … bootstrap by call"; 98 "p-value"; 99 "four times in five at the 5 % level"; 126 "elasticity"; 161 "Donut"
findings.problem: These terms are used without explanation at first use: 'the Council' (the fund's board, never introduced), 'pp', Spearman ρ / rank correlation and 'bootstrap by call' (in the header facts, before any explanation), the power phrasing, 'elasticity' and 'donut'.
findings.evidence: The first occurrences are at the listed lines. 'Spearman' appears only in the fig. 3 caption.
findings.fix: Introduce 'the Council (the fund's board that scores applications)' in the deck or at line 80, spell out 'percentage points' once, gloss ρ as 'rank correlation, -1 to +1', and describe the donut as 'leaving out projects within half a point of the line'.
findings.note: 'the Council's points' appears on lines 45 and 80 without introducing the Council. pp, ρ and 'bootstrap by call' appear in the header facts unexplained; 'Spearman' appears only in the fig. 3 caption; 'elasticity' and 'Donut' are unglossed.

findings.location: texts/film-fund.html:127 "of the 60 that never received support from these calls"
findings.problem: 'These calls' suggests 2016-2021, but the code counts later funding in any production call through 2026. Projects that changed title between applications are also not recognised as the same project, so 28 is a lower bound.
findings.evidence: analyse.py:143 later = d[d.funded & d.project.isin(near.project)], with d covering all years. project = normalized title + company.
findings.fix: Write: "never funded in any production call to 2026 under the same title and applicant (a lower bound, since retitled projects are not followed)".
